^1638. marakih] norm., mrakih N

Translation

Om̐. Let there be no obstacle.

This is the Right Behaviour ↓1 in [Performing] Observances. When you perform an observance, do not do it haphazardly, without having permission to the one who is in charge of the observances, [namely] the reverend Kaki↓2 Citragopta↓3 [and] Nini↓4 Citragopta ↓5 [The request] should be received [by means of] an offering↓6 of a white and green betel leaf on a well. The mantra is: “My Lord Kaki Citragopta and Nini Citragopta, I ask permission to perform an observance. My Lord, please accompany me when I perform an observance! Everything that I strive after, let it be obtained! If I make a mistake when performing an observance, let it be blamed on the reverend one who is in charge of the observances!” All your observances [will then be] like that.↓7 Further, the teeth-polishing leaves [have to be used] by the one who carries out the observances. The exceedingly good one is the hambulu↓8; the result is [to become] rich in gold. There are the teeth-polishing leaves of the kayәn ↓9; the result is many children. There are the teeth-polishing leaves of the vaṅkal ↓10; the result is [to become] rich in rice. There are the teeth-polishing leaves of the lampәni↓11; the result is that you are successful. The dosage of all the mixtures are the same. It is appropriate to pay full attention to it.

This is the Holy Scripture ↓12 on the Observances. Perfection in observances, its reality is bodiless. The Holy Dharma, its reality is [like] bars of hedge, for it serves as the tie with the reality of the observances [which keeps them together], and [it] also releases supernatural power.↓13 They (i.e., the observances and the Dharma) are just like the left and right bodies.↓14. The reality of observances and asceticism is likewise.↓15. That is why, one who strives to obtain goodness should perform [observances and asceticism]. [If] young people perform observances, they will obtain the result of them at a young age. There is nothing that comes into being unless it is performed; there is nothing to be taken from the arrangement [according to] what has been arranged. As if one cooks rice in the morning and eats it that morning, one cooks rice at noon and eats it that noon, one cooks rice in the evening and eats in that evening. If one is not cooking, one is not eating. [The conclusion is that] the results are according to one’s conduct. Such is the right order of [actions and results]. Because the result of bad and good conduct is obtained, that is why good conduct should be performed without delay. [This] originates from the Holy Scripture on Observances.

This is “The Detailed Enumeration of the Observances”. It should be known.

There is the observance of ‘Cutting off the Taste’ (Mәgat rasa): if one eats half [portion], and stands up ↓16 for chewing betel. It is fine if one does not speak. After chewing betel, one can eat again. Its appointed duration is one year. The deity is the Goddess Umā. The mantra is: “Om̐ Mam̐ hail to Umā!”. [I take] leave. Its result is that the love of husband and wife is not cut off, and all people love [you].

There is the observance of eating rice from slaṅgi↓17 (amaṅan sәga slaṅgi): its duration is seven months. The deity is the Goddess Vastu. The mantra is: “Om̐ hail to the Goddess Vastu!” [I take ] leave. Its result is that the love of husband and wife is not cut off, and all people↓18 love you and feel sympathy for you.

There is the observance of the ‘Earth-Leaf’ (Bhūmipāttra): if one eats without using leaves, and lays [the food] openly on earth. The deity is reverend Vaiśravaṇa. Its appointed duration is one year and seven months. The mantra is: “Om̐ hail to the illustrious↓19 Vaiśravaṇa!” [I take ] leave. Its result is being rich in land and freeholds, and you are loved by the king and priests.

There is the observance of ‘Craving to Embroider’ (Anulam iḍam)↓20: one fast all day, until the end of the day. Its appointed duration is three months. Its result is that all desires will be obtained quickly because of that. You will be beloved by men. The deity is the Reverend Brahmā. Mantra: “Om̐ Am̐ hail to Brahmā!” [I take] leave.

There is the observance of eating before the Reverend Sun goes down. Its appointed duration is three years. The deity of the observance is the Lord Śiva. Its result is that the mind will be clear. Your thoughts are alive ↓21 in one goal. Mantra: “Om̐ Mam̐ hail to Śiva!” If you apply make up.

There is the observance of not eating when the Reverend Sun is already at sunset. Its appointed duration is one year. The deity is the Reverend Śiva. The mantra is: “om̐, hail to Śiva!” [I take] leave. Its result is that one will be knowledgeable in every kind of work, especially in learning; and one will not be ignorant in playing the gamәlan ↓22, telling a story, and [composing] kakavin ↓23; one will be handsome without equal.

There is the observance of ‘Full Moon’ (Amūrṇama): you are fasting every full moon. Its appointed duration is seven years and seven months. The deity is the Goddess Ratih. Mantra: “Om̐ hail to Śrī Ratih!” [I take] leave. Its result is that your work will be successful, God and Demon will love you.

There is the observance of ‘Dark Moon’ (Nilәm): you are fasting every dark moon. Its appointed duration is seven months. The deity is the Goddess Rātri Devi. The mantra is: “Om̐ hail to Rātri Devi!” [I take] leave. Its result is that you will be loved by mankind; God and Demon will love you.

There is the observance of ‘the Abundance’ ↓24 (Narasvatī): one does not eat the cooked rice [that is cooked with] abundant water. It is only the rice cone without meat, just salt. Its appointed duration is one year and seven months. The deity is Goddess Rāja Lakṣmi. The mantra is: “Om̐ hail to Śri Rāja Lakṣmi!” [I take] leave. Its result is that your good qualities will come out, and all your aims will be fulfilled, and then you will be famous, and you will be in harmony with your spouse.

There is the observance of ‘Always in Bloom’ ↓25 (Muṣpasadā): when one should eat the flower as meat first. Its appointed duration is one year. The deity is Reverend Smara. The mantra is: “Om̐ hail to Smara!” [I take] leave. Its result is that one’s face is matchless; many [people] will love you deeply.

There is the observance of ‘Applying Salve’ (Ṅlepana): when one eats the side dish↓26 as meat first. Its appointed duration is three years. The deity is the Goddess Śrī. The mantra is: “Om̐ hail to Śrī!”. [I take] leave. Its result is your face being beautiful and calm, being rich in rice, many people will love you and have sympathy for you.

There is the observance of not chewing betel. Its appointed duration is one year, and one month. The deity is the Reverend Manodeva↓27. The mantra is: “Om̐ hail to Manodeva!” [I take] leave. Its result is that your face will be sweet [and] deeply loved, and many people will be sick with love for you

There is the observance of ‘Easy Breath’↓28 (lәga prāṇa): if one eats carrying a kris on his lap. Its appointed duration is one year and seven months. The mantra is: “Om hail to Rudra!” [I take] leave. Its result is that many people will be ready to sacrifice their lives for your life; many people will be compassionate and will love you.

There is the observance of ‘Hero’↓29 (Bīra): if one eats salt as meat. Its appointed duration is one year and three months. The deity is the Lord Iśvara. The mantra is: “Om̐ Mam̐ hail to Īśvara!” [I take] leave. Its result is that all your efforts will be achieved quickly; you will be loved by mankind, and the Gods [and] the Demons will love you.

There is the observance of not eating the betel leaf [rubbed] by lime. Its appointed duration is one year. The deity is the Goddess Bhagāvati. The mantra is: “Om̐ hail to Bhagāvati!” [I take] leave. Its result is being free from all poisons; there will be no obstacle upon you.

There is the observance of eating the leaves on which food is served. Its appointed duration is seven years. The deity is the Lord Īśvara. The mantra is: “Om̐ hail to Īśvara” ↓30. [I take] leave. Its result is to reach the heaven of Lord Īśvara. [Alternatively, if] something goes wrong, you will be reborn as a clothes vendor↓31, rich in servants, successful with the king and his minister, [and] you will not be unsurpassed by all your companions↓32.

There is the observance of ‘Eating Fruit (especially edible roots and fruits)’ (Ṅraka) ↓33: one eats every kind of fruit. Its appointed duration is three years. Its deity is the Reverend Īśvara. The mantra is: “Om̐ mam̐ hail to Śiva!” ↓34[I take] leave. Its result is reaching the abode of the Lord Śiva. [Alternatively, if] something goes wrong, you will be reborn as a wise priest, rich in silver, successful with the king and ministers.

There is the observance of ‘Behaving like Kumbhakarṇa’ (Aṅumbhakarṇa)↓35: when one sleeps on one side [position] for one year, lies on the back face up for one year, [then] lies face downwards for one year. Its appointed duration is three years. The deity of the observance is the Lord Rudra. The mantra is: Om̐ hail to Rudra! [I take] leave. Its result is that you will be loved by the learned men; all humans will respect you; all your aims will be successful.

Furthermore, if one is silent when defecating, the desire ↓36 is achieved quickly, [and] you will have many disciples.

And, if you are silent when sweeping, the result is that you will be loved by the learned man as well as gods and rulers; [your] reincarnation will be good.

And, if you are silent when polishing teeth, the result is that your purpose will be achieved.

And, if one is silent when applying the [holy] ash (bhasma), the result is that one reaches the abode of the Goddess Rātri. [Alternatively, if] something goes wrong, one is reborn as a learned man.

There is an observance when one eats following the moonlight (Anūtakәn Vulan). The technical details are as follows. On the first day after the waxing moon, [you eat only] a handful. If the waxing period of the moon increases, it [should be] added by a handful until fifteen handfuls when the full moon, because it adds a handful every day. However, on the waning moon, it should decrease by a handful every day. Finally, one fasts when the dark moon. Its appointed duration is three months. The deity is the Lord Indra. Mantra: “Om̐ salutations to god Indra!” [I take leave]. Its result is to reach the heaven of the Lord Śiva. [Alternatively, if] something goes wrong, one is reborn as a smart king, and the priest who has many disciples. 

There is the observance of ‘thursday’: the manner is one fasts every thursday. Its result is that you will be beautiful, and all your works will be good.

There is the observance of ‘Being Glow’ (Mārab) ↓37 : one should start performing the observance on the fourth day of the waxing moon. One should eat the flower of nāgasāri (Mesua ferrea), pūraṇa (Clitoria ternatea) ↓38, [and] kulalaṭa ↓39. It should end on the full moon. Its result is being handsome [or] beautiful without equal. The mantra is: ’Oṃ hail to Smara! [It is recited] when applying make-up.

There is the observance↓40 [perfomed] on the eleventh day of the waxing moon. It is called ‘beyond the smoke’ (Atikukus). Its result is becoming a brave man, [and] being perfectly prosperous.

There is the observance of eating half cooked-rice ↓41, [and] burning coconuts. Its appointed duration is fifteen days. The deity of the observance is the Reverend Viśeṣa. Its result is a beautiful head.

There is the observance of eating without using a leaf [as a plate]. Its appointed duration is seven months. Its result is that one’s actions are successful. The name of such observance is ‘Record of Victory’ (Jayapattra) ↓42.

There is an observance that over powers all [other] observances. Its result is reaching the heaven of the Lord Umapati. [Alternatively, if] something goes wrong one will reborn as a world ruler; being a powerful priest who has many disciples; having received fame as a gift.

There is the observance of being like a child who will not keep a secret. Its result is that you are not reincarnated repeatedly. [Alternatively, if] something goes wrong, one is reborn as a king.

There is the observance of putting out the fire, chewing betel for three days, [and] not eating all kinds [of food]. It is finished after three days↓43, and should be sprinkled with holy water. Its result is that all of one’s pain vanishes.

There is the observance of consuming sәsәḍĕp↓44 before the other. Its appointed duration is seven years. The deity of the observance is the Goddess Vastu. Its result is being obeyed by mankind.

There is the observance of eating the salt mix with charcoal as meat. Its result is being obeyed by mankind, being followed by the world, [and] being feared by enemies.

There is the observance of eating the [cooked rice] with four colours. Its appointed duration is five nights. Its result is becoming smart [and] powerful, and then being loved by mankind. You [will become] prominent. The name of such observance is sakabdhu ↓45

There is the observance of eating during the day, five [times] ↓46. Its result is that your fingers and skin will be fine.

There is the observance of ‘Following Interval’ (Ṅantāra): one eats in the middle of the day, [and] in the middle of the night. Its appointed duration for repeated exercise is three months. Its result is that all your descendants become powerful, [and experience] great happiness.

There is the observance of eating seven handfuls [of food] in one day. Its appointed duration to perform the observance is seven days. The name of the observance is four (Catur) ↓47. Its result↓48 is that you will be reborn as a person with a body unaffected by any type of iron in the invisible realm.

There is the observance of eating without sitting. The Reverend Hayu gives the observance. The name of the observance is the Reverend of Walking (Saṅ Hyaṅ Laku). He serves as an appearance who is beautifully attractive. Its result ↓49 is being happy in your journey; the ash of your trace is followed by attendants; you will be successful with happiness and wealth; you will enjoy the palace in the future.

There is the observance of ‘Behaving like Open Hall’ (Maṇḍapa): one eats in the lap using the leaves as a base. The Reverend Sūkṣma gives the observance. Its result is that all your deeds are fit (completely right), [and] your relationship with your spouse is not cut off. Its appointed duration is one month. The mantra is: “Om̐ hail to the [Reverend] Sūkṣma!” [I take] leave.

There is the observance of not eating all kinds of breathing beings every Pon ↓50 and Kalivon ↓51day. Its result is being obeyed by mankind.

There is the observance of eating while looking in the mirror every full moon day. Its appointed duration is one year. Its result is being reborn as a rich senior customary village head (kabayan buyut) ↓52.

This is the sacred text on the hair (Aji Rambut): one eats the black cooked rice every fourth day of the bright half of the lunar month. The mantra is: “I am performing the sacred teaching of the hair that is not red, not transparent, not white. May my hair be black just like a crow: long, soft ↓53, [and] thick. It is obtained presently. I am performing the sacred teaching of hair, which is good presently. Surely, I am performing the sacred teaching of hair. Om̐ Sa Ba Ta A I! Hail to Śiva!”

There is the observance of being silent in worship. Its result is that you will be loved by God.

There is the observance of being silent when defecating, urinating, taking a bath, applying oil, wearing undergarments, [and] walking. Its appointed duration is seven months. Lord Śiva gives the observance. [Alternatively, if] something goes wrong, one will be rich in property, rich in offspring, and be obeyed [by people], [as well as] being reborn as a minister.

In 1722 Śaka (1800 AD), on Thursday Kalivon, Vāra Marakih↓54, on the first day of the bright lunar fortnight in the month Asuji (September-October). The unit is two. The tens are two. That is the time when it is completely written.↓55

Bibliography

References

Notes

  1. ^1. According to the context of this passage, which explains the right behaviour when performing an observance, such as asking permission from the one who in charge in observance, offering betel leaves and reciting mantras, I have chosen parikramaning ‘proper order of things, right behaviour, customs (ritual) sanctioned by tradition’ (OJED, s.v.), as attested in mss. N and M. This is instead of panarima, probably a non-standard form of panariman ‘he who is given st., recipient’ (OJED, s.v.) as attested in mss. G and P, or tiṅkahiṅ panarima, meaning ‘way of acting for the recipient’ (the meaning of the word tiṅkah in OJED s.v.) as attested in ms. U. The words parikrama, panarima and tiṅkahiṅ panarima in Old Javanese have similar meanings. In the context of observance, the word parikramaniṅ brata emphasises the process of systematic conduct when performing the observance. Conversely, the word panarima brata and tiṅkahiṅ panarima brata emphasises the preparation of the practitioner before performing the observance.
  2. ^2. The word kaki means ‘grandfather; old man, elder; venerable’ (OJED, s.v.).
  3. ^3. Citragopta or Citragupta is the keeper of the records of the good and evil deeds of human beings for Yama, and as such is well-known both from Skt. and OJ. literature (his name is also given as Citragotra. In Balinese tradition, he has a famous name as Saṅ Surātma). In Kakavin Śivarātrikalpa as already mentioned by Teeuw et al. (1969: 52) he reads a book with full account of one’s deed during one’s life. In India the book is called Agrasandhāni; in the Kakavin Śivarātrikalpa it is called a galih, but no specific name is given.
  4. ^4. The word nini means ‘grandmother; woman (used in designating or addressing a religious person or an unmarried princess or girl of noble birth)’ (OJED, s.v.).
  5. ^5. The portrayal of the figure of Nini Citragopta as a female deity alongside Kaki Citragopta prior to the performance of observance in this text is particularly intriguing, as no mention of Nini Citragopta is to be found in the corpus of Old Javanese and Balinese literature. The presence of this figure brings to mind the concept of śakti in Śaivism. This is one of the key elements indicating the presence of a tantric spirit within this text.
  6. ^6. I have chosen to use the word caru rather than the abbreviation ca as the abbreviation because it is not commonly found in the corpus of Old Javanese literature. Furthermore, by using the word caru, which means ‘to have (make, present) as an offering’ (OJED, s.v.), will help readers to understand the meaning of the term directly.
  7. ^7. By asking permission to the Kaki Citragopta and Nini Citragopta, practitioners of the observance simultaneously seek protection from them. If they commit a mistake, that mistake is attributed to this deity. This appears to be a tactic employed by practitioners to ensure their safety while performing the observance.
  8. ^8. Hambulu, ambulu is a particular kind of tree, of the ficus family (Jb.: Ficus infectoria) (OJED, s.v.).
  9. ^9. Kayәn is a particular kind of tree and its flowers. In bal. com. used to render kuyaṅ, q.v. (OJED, s.v.).
  10. ^10. Vaṅkal is a particular kind of (wild) tree (KBW: a variety of mimosa) (OJED, s.v.).
  11. ^11. Lampәni is a shrub plant that is about two meters high, the leaves are oval in shape, the young fruit tastes sour, while the old ones taste sweet and are dark red; (KBI, 2016: 717).
  12. ^12. The word tattva derived from Sanskrit has many meanings. The OJED defines it as ‘what something is in fact; the facts of the matter; how it really happened; the true story; the essential; the actual; the various categories of reality according to Sāmkhya doctrine; the doctrine concerning reality; the philosophy; the writings containing this doctrine; and really or in reality’ (OJED, s.v.). In this context, I have translated the word tattva as ‘holy scripture’, equating it with dharma and jñāna in Old Javanese. Acri (2018: 9) has provided a detailed explanation of the meaning of tattva and jñāna as ‘scripture’ in Old Javanese and Sanskrit sources to support this argument.
  13. ^13. This passage discusses the relationship between brata‘the observance’ and dharma ‘the truth’. The text explains that the reality of perfection in observances is bodiless. This is why it needs the holy truth as its body to hold everything together. Metaphorically, the truth is referred to as ‘the bars of a hedge’. Here, the metaphor ‘bars of hedge’ indicates that the truth acts as a ‘barrier’ to ensure that, after obtaining supernatural power, the practitioner of the observance still behaves in daily life under the light of Dharma and uses his supernatural power for kindness.
  14. ^14. The left body refers to the ‘observances‘ (brata), and the right body refers to the ‘holy truth‘ (dharma). The two concepts complement each other
  15. ^15. There are two interpretations regarding the use of the word ‘tapa’ here. Firstly, the word ‘tapa’ may be used in parallel with the word ‘dharma’ (‘holy truth’), as explained in the previous sentence. Secondly, the word tapa is actually used in conjunction with the word brata (‘observance’). OJED (s.v.) explains that the word tapa means ‘religious austerity, bodily mortification, penance, asceticism’. Often in combination with brata, either ‘the observance of asceticism (penance)’ or ‘penance and other religious observances’.
  16. ^16. The literal meaning of the word sumĕṅka is ‘to go upwards, rise, climb’ (OJED s.v.). In this passage, I have translated it more liberal as ‘stand up’.
  17. ^17. I have choosen the word slaṅgi as attested in ms. U in the Balinese, which means ‘a pyramid-shaped structure made of aren palm or jackfruit leaves used to display rice during the Kuningan festival’ (KBI, 2016: 987). I have not found the meaning of the word ṅgi attested in ms. G and N, as well as the word ṅgi as attested in ms. M, nor of gaṅgi as attested in ms. P.
  18. ^18. I have emended the phrase sama janma attested in G M N U and janma kabeh attested in P to samanta janma ‘all people’. I made this decision in the light of previous passage 3.1 mvaṅ samanta janma paḍa sih ‘and all people love [you]’.
  19. ^19. have chosen the word śrī, which is attested in P, instead of Śram̐ in G, Sam̐ in M and N, and Śi in U. This is because in other passages of this text, such as 3.7 om̐ śrī ratih devyai namaḥ, 3.10 om̐ śrī smarāya namaḥ, 3.11 om̐ śrī śrī devyai namaḥ, etc., the word śrī is used instead of the other bījamantra. The bījamantras like śram̐ in G, sam̐ in M and N, and śi are not appropriate in this context. In the Indian tradition, the reverend Vaiśravaṇa is often identified with Kubera. He is the guardian of the northern direction and his home is in the northern quadrant of the topmost tier of the lower half of Mount Meru.
  20. ^20. I have conjectured nulam idhan in G, nulam iḍam in M, N and U, and nulambhi nan in P to anulam iḍam ‘craving to embroider’. This word has been conjectured to convey the proper meaning in Old Javanese. The word anulam is derived from the word sulam, meaning ‘to embroider’ (OJED s.v.), and the word iḍam means ‘to experience the cravings of pregnancy, to be pregnant’ (OJED s.v.). Thus, the word anulam iḍam can be translated as ‘craving to embroider’.
  21. ^21. In this context, the phrase ‘thought will be alive’ refers to a state of mind full of inspiration. It is also suitable with the technique of the observance that has a link to the Reverend Sun as the origin of all light in this world, and is also in accordance with the belief that the Reverend Sun is the origin of all light in this world.
  22. ^22. Gamәlan is percussion instrument, ensemble of percussion instruments (OJED, s.v.).
  23. ^23. Kakavin is poem (in Indian metres) (OJED, s.v.).
  24. ^24. In the light of Sanskrit (Monier-Williams, 1182), I translate the name of this observance, Narasvatī, as ‘the abundance’ instead of ‘acting like Sarasvatī’, due to the absence of a link between Sarasvatī, the goddess of knowledge, and the deity and mantra in this observance. According to the deity of this passage, Rāja Lakṣmi, who is revered as the goddess of happiness, fortune, wealth, prosperity, beauty, fertility, sovereignty and abundance, this translation is appropriate.
  25. ^25. Other posibility to translate this term are ‘always worshiping with flowers’, ‘always arranging flowers’, and ‘always wearing flowers’.
  26. ^26. In Modern Javanese, the word lalab refers to ‘uncooked fruit and leaves eaten with rice’ (OJED, s.v.), whereas in Balinese, it refers to ‘boiled food’ (KBI, 2016: 290).
  27. ^27. I have choosen the word manodeva attested in ms. M and N, rather than aśvino attested in ms. G; asvido attested in ms. P; and maṣnodeva attested in ms. U because the word manodeva is quite similar to Manobhava as the god of love (see OJED s.v.). This phenomenon is probably similar to the localisation of the god Manobhu in the context of Bali. The word manodeva is also appropriate to the dative mantra manodevāya when compared to the others in this passage. Another important reason is that the result of this observance is meṅət rūpanta manis, mvaṅ akveh bhrānta hyun iri kita: ‘your face will be sweet and deeply loved, and many people will fall in love with you.’ This result of the observance is strongly related to the Manobhava as mentioned in 3.10 riṅ rūpa tan pasiriṅ, akveh rәsəp asih iri kita, and 3.203 pinakarūpa, aśrī sumilah.
  28. ^28. Another alternative translation of Lәga Prāṇa is ‘Contented Life’. Literally, the word lәga means ‘open, satisfied, content, relieved; taking lightly, accepting, renouncing readily’ (OJED s.v.), and the word prāṇa means ‘1. breath; first of the five vital airs (see pañcabāyu); 2. the breath of life, life; 3. (as a seat of the feelings:) heart, soul; 4. the place on the body where one can be mortally wounded (where one’s life is located), esp. the breast; mortal (of a wound); 5. numeral coefficient for living creatures’ (OJED s.v.).
  29. ^29. I assume that the word bīra here is the other form of vīra which is refers to brave man, hero, valiant warrior; brave, valiant (OJED s.v.). This phenomenon is often in Old Javanese, for instance the word bulan ‘moon’ also has other form as vulan.
  30. ^30. An interesting textual phenomenon can be observed here. The mss. M, N and U contain the mantra: om̐ mam̐ īśvarāya namaḥ, whereas G contains the mantra: mantra kadi ṅuni, meaning ‘the mantra is as before’. This phenomenon goes beyond lexical synonymy, but is a synonym in syntax scope. The ms. G refers to a previous mantra that already exists in the initial passage (4v-5r), which contains om̐ mam̐ iśvarāya namaḥ.
  31. ^31. I have chosen the word basana in ms. G instead of the word bhāṣa because of the parallel with the MM in passage 5 (hana brata akarvan patrāhāra ṅaranya, pituṅ tahun samayanya, ⟨phalanya⟩ mulih mariṅ svarga saṅ hyaṅ iśvara, sasarnya ajanma riṅ juru basana, sugih hulun, labdha ri saṅ prabhu.). The word basana in was derived from the Sanskrit word vasana ‘clothes, garment, attire’ (see OJED, s.v.).
  32. ^32. Lexically, the sentence tan pada lavan rovaṅta kabeh can be translated as ‘you will not be equal to all your companions’. I translated this sentence more liberal as ‘unsurpassed by all your companions’.
  33. ^33. I have choosen the word ṅraka as attested in mss. M N and U as a kind of a vernacular form of Old Javanese in Bali which is not attested in OJED. However, the meaning is the same with the word araka which means ‘taking, seizing, robbing, food (esp. edible roots and fruit?)’ as attested in ms. G.
  34. ^34. Mss. M P and U contains the mantra: om̐ mam̐ ⟨śivā⟩ya namaḥ svāhā, whereas the ms. G contains mantra kadi ṅūni. See my footnote in passage 3.16.
  35. ^35. This observance is interesting because it imitates the behavior of Kumbhakarṇa as a young brother of Rāvāṇa in the Rāmāyaṇa epic. On the basis of Kakavin Rāmāyaṇa, the figure of Kumbhakarṇa is always sleeping. However he woke up when he heard the quintessence speech of his grandfather. The Kakavin Rāmāyaṇa mentions the figure of Kumbhakarṇa as follows: Kāla saṅ kaki sәḍәṅ mavara-varah, Kumbhakarṇa sira jagra ya rumәṅə̄, de nikari ujar-ujar pasili-silih, śīghra yar pavuṅu arddha warurutәn. When his grandfather was giving his admonishment, Kumbhakarṇa woke up, and on hearing the conversation quickly became attentive, though still very sleepy (see Santoso, 1980: 358).
  36. ^36. I have translated the word prih as ‘desire’, as this is its meaning in Balinese (KBI, 2016: 730). OJED (s.v.) defines the word prih as ‘effort, exertion, full attention, great care and devotion’.
  37. ^37. I have conjectured the word mūrāba as mārab, as the former does not appear in the OJED or Balinese dictionaries. I assume that mūraba is a mystical form of mārab, which means ‘to flare, flame, blaze, glow’ (OJED, s.v.). It is also consistent with the technique of performing the observance, whereby the practitioner eats certain types of flowers.
  38. ^38. Nāgasāri: According to the text titled Kavi Jānaki, collected in Unit Lontar, Udayana University. I found the word purāṇa used to designate one plant, namely itil. The text contains: krĕntikā, smaracatrā, wagaprańā, puranā, gamantya ṅa itil (Kavi Jānaki, 16r). In the oral tradition, the word itil refers to the talaṅ flower (Clitoria ternatea).
  39. ^39. I have not found the specific plant to which kulalaṭa refers. OJED (s.v.) explains that lalaṭa is a particular kind of flower or floral motif.
  40. ^40. This passage does not provide a detailed explanation of the technique for performing the observance. I assume that the word mopavāsa ‘fasting’ is needed here to complete the explanation. The word brata itself also has the meaning of a ‘holy practice’ (fasting, continence, etc.) (OJED, s.v.).
  41. ^41. I translate aron-aron as ‘half-cooked rice’ rather than ‘with leaves’ (variant form of aron-ron). I assume the word aron-aron was derived from the words haru or aru. In Old Javanese, haru-daṅ means ‘a pot for half-cooked rice’ and paṅarvan means ‘a pot in which half-cooked rice is stirred before being put back in the kukusan’ (ModJ) (OJED, s.v.). In Balinese, the words haru/aru + -an become aruwan/aron (another instance for this sound change is: kalaṅvan → kalaṅon/kalaṅәn, vvaṅ → voṅ, etc. ), meaning ‘half-cooked rice’.
  42. ^42. OJED (s.v.) defines the term jayapattra as ‘a record of victory (in a lawsuit) given to the victorious party’. In this context, I only use ‘record of victory’ to make the translation jayapattra more precise.
  43. ^43. Other alternatives for this translation is ‘the food is taken after abstinence for three days’.
  44. ^44. Sәsәḍep is finely chopped betel etc with dadap leaves, bras and kuñit used as bhasma on the temples, between the eyes, on the head and the shoulder-blades (esp. in certain ceremonies) (OJED s.v.)
  45. ^45. The word sakabdhu does not exist in OJED and Balinese dictionaries. I have not found any interpretations of this word yet.
  46. ^46. The number 5 in the text is not clearly explained. For the time being, this number 5 is interpreted as ‘5 times’. I put it in the brackets. Another possibility is ‘5 handfuls of food per day’.
  47. ^47. I have not found yet the releation between the name of this observance catur ‘four’ with the technique to perform the observance and the duration.
  48. ^48. For the reason in adding the word pha, in this passage see footnote 3.331.
  49. ^49. I have added the word pha, meaning ‘its result’ in accordance with the general pattern found in other passages of the Tattva Brata. Pha is typically placed after the mantra portion: ma, om̐ śambhave namaḥ, pamit, pha, mañjanma riṅ kulaputra (3.26); after the duration of the brata: tigaṅ tahun lavasnya, pha, drәman aputra, siṅ prih meṅgal katəkan (3.27); after the technical details of the brata’s performance: hana brata tan pamaṅan ivak bavi, pha, tan kataman deniṅ sarvaviṣya (3.63), after the name of the brata: saṅ hyaṅ kr̥ta bhuvana hyaṅniṅ brata, pha, etc. (3.87).
  50. ^50. Pon is the third day in the five-day cycle (pañcavāra) of the Old Javanese/Balinese calendar system.
  51. ^51. Kalivon is the fifth day in the five-day cycle (pañcavāra) of the Old Javanese/Balinese calendar system.
  52. ^52. The word kabayan means ‘old; an elder, chief, leader’ (OJED, s.v.), while buyut means ‘great-grandfather, great-grandchild; elder’ (OJED, s.v.). In the Balinese context, the word kabayan refers to a ‘customary village head’ (KBI, 2016: 96). For this reason, in this context, I translate kabayan buyut as ‘senior customary village head’.
  53. ^53. I have emended the word alambas to alәmәs. The Balinese word alambas meaning ‘long’ (KBI, 2016: 540) is already expressed by the word adavā ‘long’ (OJED, s.v.) in the previous word in this sentence. The word alәmәs meaning ‘pliant, lithe, lissom, supple, slender, and soft’ (OJED, s.v.) is a more suitable choice in this context as the main topic is about the hair.
  54. ^54. Marakih is the name of the 16th vuku (OJED, s.v.)
  55. ^55. This manuscript was completed at the end of the 18th century.

.<!-- G hana brata cakravratti, ṅa, vr̥tti ginave cakrā rūpa, panunu skul saśirahniṅ vanāra gə̄ṅnya, yan kalanta maṅa _ _ pasaṅ taṅ vr̥ti, tumpaṅakniṅ skul, saśirahniṅ vanara gə̄ṅnya, Umar̥p vetan kita maṅan, hayva pjah hikaṅ vr̥ti, pavusan kita maṅan, yan ahurip ikaṅ vr̥ti, huvusakәn denta maṅan, _ _ _, nya, meṅgal asiṅ sakaryyanta, siddhā katmū sapinakṣa, subaga kita, kinasihaniṅ pāṇḍita, mvaṅ saṅ prabhu, r̥si padha sih kabeh -->

.<!-- M hana brata candrāvr̥tti, ṅa, ginave candrā rūpa, panunu skul saśirah iṅ vanara gə̄ṅnyā, yan kalanta maṅan, pasaṅ taṅ vr̥tti, tumpaṅākniṅ skul, saśirah iṅ vanara gə̄ṅnya, Umar̥p vetan kita pamaṅan, yan mati ghni hika vr̥ti, havusanā dentāmaṅan, pha, siṅ karyyanta meṅgal siddha katmu siṅ pinakṣa, subhagā kittha, kinasiha niṅ saṅ pāṇdhita, mvaṅ saṅ prabhū, r̥sәp āsih kabeh -->
.
2175<!-- N hana brata, candrāvr̥tti, ṅa, ginave candrā rūpā, panunu skul saśirahiṅ vanara gə̄ṅnya, yan kalanta maṅan, pasaṅ taṅ vr̥tti, tumpaṅakniṅ skul¸ saśirahiṅ vanarā, Umar̥p vetan kita pamaṅan, yan mati ghni hika riṅ vr̥tti, havusāna denta amaṅan, pha, siṅ karyyanta meṅgal katmu sidḍa siṅ pinakṣa, subhagā kittha, kinasihaniṅ saṅ pāṅḍita, mvaṅ saṅ prabhū, r̥sǝp asih kabeh -->
.
.<!-- P hana brata ñakravartti, ṅa. vr̥ti ginave cakrā rūpānya manunu sәkul sasirahiṅ vanara gәṅnya, yan kālaniṅ amaṅan pasaṅ hikaṅ vr̥tti, tumpaṅakna riṅ sәkul, śirahniṅ vanara gәṅnya humar̥p vetan, kita amaṅan, hayva pәjah hikaṅ vr̥tti, husan kita amaṅan, yan hurip hikaṅ vrti huvusakna dlәntāmaṅan, phalanya siṅ sakāryyanta siddha katәmu saṅ pinakṣanta, subhaga kitā, kinaptihan deniṅ pāṇdhitā mvaṅ saṅ prabhu, r̥ṣi kabeh holasih -->
.
.<!-- U hana brata candravr̥ti, ṅa, ginave candra rupa, panunu skul ṣasirah iṅ vānarā gə̄ṅnya, yan kālantāmaṅan savataṅ vr̥ti, tumpaṅakәn iṅ skul, sasirah iṅ vānāra, Umakar̥p vetan sira maṅan, hayva pjah ikaṅ vr̥tti yapvan pjah ikaṅ vr̥tti, pahuvusan kita maṅān, yan urip ikaṅ vr̥tthi, huvusakәn dentāmaṅan, pha, siṅ kāryyanta meṅgal, sidda kitā siṅ pinakṣa, subhaggā kita, kinasiha niṅ pāṇdhita, mvaṅ saṅ prabhu, r̥sәp hasih kabeh -->
2180
.<!-- kata agni dinormalisasi-->
.
.<div type="subchapter" n="3.42">
.<ab xml:id="tattvabrata_42">
2185hana brata
. <app><lem wit="#M #N #U">candra vr̥tti</lem><rdg wit="#G">cakravratti</rdg><rdg wit="#P">ñakravartti</rdg></app>,
. <app><lem wit="#M #N #U"><abbr>ṅa</abbr>, ginave</lem><rdg wit="#G #P" cause="additive">ṅa, vr̥tti ginave</rdg></app>
. <app><lem wit="#M #N #U">candra</lem><rdg wit="#G #P">cakra</rdg></app>
. <app><lem wit="#G #M #N #U">rūpa</lem><rdg wit="#P">rūpanya</rdg></app>,
2190 <app><lem wit="#P">manunu</lem><rdg wit="#G #M #N #U">panunu</rdg></app>
. sәkul saśirahiṅ vānara gə̄ṅnya, yan
. <app><lem wit="#G #M #N #U">kālanta</lem><rdg wit="#P">kālaniṅ</rdg></app>
. <app><lem wit="#G #M #N #U">maṅan</lem><rdg wit="#P">amaṅan</rdg></app>,
. pasaṅ taṅ vr̥tti, tumpaṅakәn iṅ sәkul, saśirahiṅ vānara,
2195 <app><lem wit="#G #M #N #P">umarәp</lem><rdg wit="#U">umakarәp</rdg></app>
. vetan kita
. <app><lem wit="#G #P #U">maṅan</lem><rdg wit="#M #N">apaṅan</rdg></app>,
. <app><lem wit="#M #N">yan mati</lem><rdg wit="#G #P #U">hayva pәjah agni</rdg></app>
. <app><lem wit="#N">ika riṅ vr̥tti</lem><rdg wit="#G #P #U">ikaṅ vr̥ti</rdg><rdg wit="#M">ika vr̥ti</rdg></app>,
2200 <app><lem wit="#M #N">avusana denta amaṅan</lem><rdg wit="#G #U">pavusan kita maṅan, yan ahurip ikaṅ vr̥ti, huvusakәn denta maṅan</rdg><rdg wit="#P">husan kita amaṅan, yan hurip hikaṅ vr̥ti huvusakna dlәntāmaṅan</rdg><rdg wit="#U">pahuvusan kita maṅan, yan urip ikaṅ vr̥tthi, huvusakәn dentāmaṅan</rdg>
.</app>,
. <abbr>pha</abbr>,
. <app><lem wit="#M #N #U">siṅ kāryanta meṅgal, </lem><rdg wit="#G" cause="transposition">meṅgal asiṅ sakāryanta</rdg><rdg wit="#P">siṅ sakārynta</rdg></app>
. <app><lem wit="#M">siddha katәmu siṅ pinakṣa,</lem><rdg wit="#G">siddha katәmu sapinakṣa</rdg><rdg wit="#N">katәmu siddha siṅ pinakṣa</rdg><rdg wit="#P">katәmu saṅ pinakṣanta</rdg><rdg wit="#U">sidda kita siṅ pinakṣa</rdg></app>
2205 subhaga kita,
. <app><lem wit="#G #M #N #U">kinasihaniṅ</lem><rdg wit="#P">kinaptihan</rdg></app>
. <app><lem wit="#M #N">saṅ paṇḍita</lem><rdg wit="#G #U">pāṇdhita</rdg><rdg wit="#P">deniṅ pāṇdhitā</rdg>
. </app>,
. mvaṅ saṅ prabhu,
2210 <app><lem wit="#M #N #U">rәsǝp asih kabeh</lem><rdg wit="#G">r̥si padha sih kabeh</rdg><rdg wit="#P">r̥ṣi kabeh olasih.</rdg></app>
. <app><lem wit="#G #M #N #P #U"></lem><note> hana brata, candrāvr̥tti,... asih kabeh<ptr target="#G"/>
. in 3.40 <ptr target="#M"/>
. in 3.42 <ptr target="#N"/>
. in 3.42 <ptr target="#P"/>
2215 in 3.41 <ptr target="#U"/>
. in 3.40 </note>
.</app>
.</ab>
.</div>
2220
.
.<!-- G hana brāta harakta, ṅa, amaṅan laktan baṅ, satahun divasanya, phalanya, mantukiṅ svargga bhaṭāra brahmā, sasārnya maṅjanma vvaṅ bhaṇyaga sugih -->
.
.<!-- M hana brata ṅraktā, ṅa, amaṅan ktan bāṅ, satavun divasanyā, pha, siṅ karyyanta siddha, mvaṅ mantukiṅ svarggā bhaṭāra brahmā, sasārnya mañjanmā riṅ vvaṅ baṇyagā sugih -->
2225
.<!-- N hana brata ṅrakta, ṅa, amaṅan laktan bāṅ, satahun divaśanya, pha, siṅ karyyanta sidḍa, mvaṅ mantukiṅ svargga bhaṭāra brahmā, sasarnya mañjanmā riṅ baṇyaga sugih -->
.
.<!-- P hana brata ṅrakta, ṅa, amaṅan kәtan bāṅ, satahun ṣamayanya, phalanya mantukiṅ svarggān bhaṭāra brahmā, sasarnya mañjanma riṅ voṅ bhagya hasugih-->
.
2230<!-- U hana brata ṅrakta, ṅa, amaṅan laktan bāṅ, satahun divaṣanya, pha, siṅ kāryyanta siddā, mvaṅ mantukiṅ svargga bhāṭāra brāhmā, sasarnya maṅjanma riṅ vvaṅ banyā sugih -->
.
.<div type="subchapter" n="3.43">
.<ab xml:id="tattvabrata_43">
.hana brata
2235 <app><lem wit="#M #N #P #U">ṅrakta</lem><rdg wit="#G">arakta</rdg></app>,
. <abbr>ṅa,</abbr>
. amaṅan
. <app><lem wit="#G #N #U">lakәtan</lem><rdg wit="#M #P">kәtan</rdg></app>
. baṅ, satahun divasanya,
2240 <abbr>pha</abbr>,
. <app><lem wit="#M #N #U">siṅ kāryanta siddha</lem><rdg wit="#G #P"><gap reason="omitted"></gap></rdg></app>,
. <app><lem wit="#M #N #U">mvaṅ</lem><rdg wit="#G #P"><gap reason="omitted"></gap></rdg></app>
. mantuk iṅ
. <app><lem wit="#G #M #N #U">svarga</lem><rdg wit="#P">svargan</rdg></app>
2245 bhaṭāra brahmā, sasarnya
. <app><lem wit="#M #N #P">mañjanma</lem><rdg wit="#G #U">maṅjanma</rdg></app>
. riṅ
. <app><lem wit="#N">baṇyaga sugih</lem><rdg wit="#G #M">vvaṅ baṇyaga sugih</rdg><rdg wit="#P">voṅ bhagya asugih</rdg><rdg wit="#U">va banya sugih</rdg></app>.
.<app>

.<note> hana brata ṅrakta ... baṇyaga sugih
.<ptr target="#G"/>
. in 3.41 <ptr target="#M"/>
. in 3.43 <ptr target="#N"/>
2255 in 3.43 <ptr target="#P"/>
. in 3.42 <ptr target="#U"/>
. in 3.41 </note>
.</app>
.</ab>
2260</div>
.
.
.<!-- G hana brata durggā, ṅa, amaṅan skul jahli, limaṅṅ lek samayanya, phalanya, mantukiṅ svarggā bhaṭāra viṣṇu, sasarnya paṅjanma riṅ viku bahu sisya kita-->
.<!-- M hana bratandurggā, ṅa, amaṅan skul jali, limaṅ lek samayanyā, pha, mantukiṅ svarggā bhaṭāra viṣṇu, sasārnya mañjanmā riṅ viku bahusiṣya -->
2265<!-- N hana brata ndurgga, ṅa, amaṅan skül jali, limāṅ lek ṣamayanya, pha, mantukiṅ svārgga bhaṭāra viṣṇu, sasārnya mañjanmā riṅ viku bahu sisya-->
.<!-- P hana brata dūrgga, ṅaranya amaṅan sәkul jali, limaṅ lek ṣamayanya, phalanya mantukiṅ bhaṭāra viṣṇu, sasarnya mañjadma riṅ viku bhahu siṣya, kitā-->
.<!-- U hana brata ndurgga, ṅa, amaṅan skul juli, limaṅ lek samayanya, pha, mantuk iṅ svargga bhaṭāra viṣṇu, sasarnya maṅjanma riṅ viku bāhu śiṣya-->
.
.<div type="subchapter" n="3.44">
2270<ab xml:id="tattvabrata_44">
.hana brata
. <app><lem wit="#G #U">durga</lem><rdg wit="#M #N #U">ndurga</rdg></app>,
. <abbr>ṅa,</abbr>
. amaṅan sәkul

. limaṅ lek samayanya,
. <abbr>pha</abbr>,

2280 bhaṭāra viṣṇu, sasarnya
. <app><lem wit="#M #N">mañjanma</lem><rdg wit="#G">paṅjanma</rdg><rdg wit="#P">mañjadma</rdg><rdg wit="#U">maṅjanma</rdg></app>
. riṅ viku bahu
. <app><lem wit="#M #N #U">śiṣya</lem><rdg wit="#G #P">sisya kita</rdg></app>.

.
.
.<!-- G hana brāta kanaka drāva, ṅa, amaṅan skul kuniṅ, tigaṅ tahun samayanya, phalanya, mantukiṅ svarggā bhaṭāra saṅ mahadeva, sasarnya _ _ nma riṅ dhampvavaṅ sugih -->
.
2300<!-- M hana brata kanakā drava, ṅa, amaṅan sga kuniṅ, tigaṅ tavun samayanya, pha, mantukiṅ svarggā saṅ hyaṅ mahādevā, sasārnya mañjanmā riṅ dampvavaṅ sugih -->
.
.<!-- N hana brata kanaka drava, ṅa, amaṅan skul kuniṅ, tigaṅ tahun samayanya, pha, mantukiṅ svargga saṅ hyaṅ mahādeva, sasarnya mañjanma riṅ dampvavaṅ sugih-->
.
.<!-- P hana brata kanakadravā, ṅa, hamagan sәkul kuniṅ, tigaṅ tavun samayanya, phalanya mantukiṅ svarggān bhaṭāra mahādeva, sasarnya mañjanma riṅ vvaṅ sugih -->
2305
.<!-- U hana brata kanaka drāvā, ṅa, amaṅan skul kuniṅ, tigaṅ tahun samayanya, pha, mantuk iṅ svargga sa hyaṅ mahādeva, sasarnya maṅjanma riṅ dampvavaṅ sugih -->
.
.<div type="subchapter" n="3.45">
.<ab xml:id="tattvabrata_45">
2310hana brata kanaka drava,
. <abbr>ṅa,</abbr>
. amaṅan
. <app><lem wit="#G #N #P #U">sәkul</lem><rdg wit="#M" cause="lexical">sәga</rdg></app>

2315 <abbr>pha</abbr>,
. mantuk iṅ
. <app><lem wit="#G #M #N #U">svarga</lem><rdg wit="#G">svargan</rdg></app>
. <app><lem wit="#M #N">saṅ hyaṅ</lem><rdg wit="#G #P">bhaṭāra</rdg><rdg wit="#U">sa hyaṅ</rdg></app>
. mahādeva, sasarnya
2320 <app><lem wit="#M #N #P">mañjanma</lem><rdg wit="#G">_ _nma</rdg><rdg wit="#U">maṅjanma</rdg></app>

.
.
.<!-- G hana brāta phalahara, ṅa, amaṅan sarvva phala, tigaṅ lek samayanya, phalanya mantukiṅ padha bhaṭāra sāddhā śiva, sasarnya maṅjanma riṅ janma sugih bahu vadva -->
.
2340<!-- M hana brata phalahāra, ṅa, amaṅan sarvva phalā, tigāṅ lek ṣamayanyā, pha, mantukiṅ svārgga bhaṭāra śaddha śiva, sasārnya mañjanma riṅ vvaṅ sugih bahu siṣya, bahu vadvā -->
.
.<!-- N hana brata phalahāra, ṅa, amaṅan sarvva phalā, tigāṅ lek ṣamayanya, pha, mantukiṅ svargga bhaṭāra śadḍā śiva, sasarnya mañjanma riṅ vvaṅ sugih, bahu sisya, bahu vadva -->
.
.<!-- U hana brata phalahāra, ṅa, amaṅanhā sarvva phala, tigaṅṅ lek samayanya, pha, mantuk iṅ svargga bhaṭāra sadā śiva, sasarnya maṅjanma riṅ vvaṅ sugih saṅkan rare, listvahayu paripūrṇna -->
2345
.<div type="subchapter" n="3.46">
.<ab xml:id="tattvabrata_46">
.hana brata phala āhāra,
. <abbr>ṅa,</abbr>
2350 <app><lem wit="#G #M #N">amaṅan</lem><rdg wit="#U">amaṅanha</rdg></app>

. <abbr>pha</abbr>,

. <app><lem wit="#M #N #U">svarga</lem><rdg wit="#G" cause="lexical">padha</rdg></app>

. <app><lem wit="#M #N">mañjanma</lem><rdg wit="#G #U" cause="morphological">maṅjanma</rdg></app>
. riṅ
. <app><lem wit="#M #N #U">vvaṅ</lem><rdg wit="#G">janma</rdg></app>
. <app><lem wit="#G #M #N">sugih</lem><rdg wit="#U" cause="additive">sugih saṅkan rare</rdg></app>,
2360 <app><lem wit="#M #N">bahuśiṣya</lem><rdg wit="#G"><gap reason="omitted"></gap></rdg><rdg wit="#U">listvahayu paripūrṇna</rdg></app>,

.
.

.
.<!-- M hana bratandumā, ṅa, tan pamaṅan tampakiṅ ṅapuy, tigāṅ tavun samayanya, pha, mantukiṅ svārggā bhaṭāra brahmā, sasārnya mañjanmā riṅ vvaṅ sugih saṅkan rare, listvayu paripūrṇna-->
.
.<!-- N hana bratandumā, ṅa, tan pamaṅan tampakiṅ apuy, tigaṅ tahun samayanya, pha, mantukiṅ svargga bhaṭāra brahmā, sasārnya mañjanmā riṅ vvaṅ sugih saṅkan rare, listvayu paripūrṅna-->
2380
.<!-- P hana brata, ndumā, ṅa, tan pamaṅan huryyaniṅ hapuy, phalanya, mulih riṅ svarggan bhaṭāra Iśvarā, mañjanma riṅ kula putra riṅ dlahā-->
.
.<div type="subchapter" n="3.47">
.<ab xml:id="tattvabrata_47">
2385hana brata ndhūma,
. <abbr>ṅa,</abbr> tan pamaṅan

. apuy,
. <app><lem wit="#G #M #N">tigaṅ tahun samayanya</lem><rdg wit="#P"><gap reason="omitted"></gap></rdg></app>,
2390 <abbr>pha</abbr>,
. <app><lem wit="#G #M #N">mantuk iṅ</lem><rdg wit="#P" cause="lexical">mulih riṅ</rdg></app>
. <app><lem wit="#G #M #N">svarga</lem><rdg wit="#P">svargan</rdg></app>
. bhaṭāra
. <app><lem wit="#G #M #N">brahmā</lem><rdg wit="#P">iśvarā</rdg></app>,

.<note> hana bratanduma ... listvayu paripūrṇa
.<ptr target="#G"/>

. in 3.79 </note>

.</ab>
.</div>
2410
.<!-- G hana brāta ṅalivon, ṅa, moliha pituṅ tumpәk kalivon, phalanya, prih maṅgal katmu -->
.<!-- M hana brata ṅalivon, ṅa, moliha pituṅ tumpәk kalivon, pha, prih meṅgal katmu -->
.<!-- N hana brata ṅalivon, ṅa, molihā pituṅ tumpǝkalivon, pha, prih meṅgal katmu -->
.<!-- P -->
2415<!-- U hana brata ṅalivon, ṅa, moliha pituṅ tumpәk kalivon, pha, prih meṅgal katmu -->
.
.<div type="subchapter" n="3.48">
.<ab xml:id="tattvabrata_48">

2420 <abbr>ṅa,</abbr>
. moliha pituṅ tumpǝk kalivon,
. <abbr>pha</abbr>,
. prih meṅgal katәmu.

. in 3.45 </note>
.</app>

2435

.<!-- N hana brata maṅan sarvva vijā, mvaṅ pucukiṅ halalaṅ, pha, vāk bhajra, sidḍi mantra, jaya kitthā -->
.<!-- U hana brata maṅan sarvva vijā, muvaṅ pucuk iṅ alaṅ ṅalaṅ, pha, vak bajra, siddi mantrā, jaya si kita -->
2440
.<div type="subchapter" n="3.49">

. <app><lem wit="#M #N #U">vīja</lem><rdg wit="#G" cause="additive">vija, ṅa</rdg></app>,

.

. sugih ḷmah sima, vr̥ddhi kadaṅ varggānta makveh -->

.<!-- M hana brata bhūmi patra, ṅa, yan amaṅan tan pahrāyyan, saṅaṅ tavun samayanyā, pha, kasambhega deniṅ saṅ pāṇdhitā,

.<ab>
. hana brata
3360<app>
.<lem type="conj">godhara</lem>
.<rdg wit="#M #N">kodara</rdg>
.</app>,
. <abbr>ṅa</abbr>,
3365 savulan lavasnya,
.<app>
.<lem type="norm">amvitana i</lem>
.<rdg wit="#M #N">amvitane</rdg>
.</app>
3370 taṅgal
.<app>
.<lem wit="#N">pisan</lem>
.<rdg wit="#M">apisan</rdg>
.</app>
3375 iṅ karo, tan pamaṅana sarvaprāṇi, mvaṅ salviriṅ vijiliṅ sāgara, śāntaveṣa ta kita, mavastra piṅe, agәgәlaṅa lave kinuniran, taṅan tәṅǝn, hayva mamati-mati sarvāmbәkan,</ab>
.
. <ab> makacarunya
.<app>
.<lem type="emn">amvita</lem>
3380<rdg wit="#M #N">mvitā</rdg>
.</app>
. brata, sәkul iṅ tamas, ulamana sarvagaṅan, vaḍah limas, tuhuṅ salvirnya, papare, baligo, sambǝl, salviranya tan patarasi, gogoreṅan
.<app>
.<lem wit="#N">kolentaṅ</lem>
3385<rdg wit="#M">kolantaṅ</rdg>
.</app>, cacaṅanon ginoreṅ, mvaṅ papare ginoreṅ, padha ǝmbanana sasavi, hǝmba sakalor, huvus ratǝṅ tumpaṅakәn iṅ sәkul iṅ tamas, makadi yan ana pәhan, miñak, mavaḍah limas, den aśrī
.<app>
.<lem wit="#M">deniṅ aniṅkah</lem>
.<rdg wit="#N">deniṅkah</rdg>
3390</app>
.<!-- caru, sәḍah voh,-->
.<app>
.<lem wit="#N">raka</lem>
.<rdg wit="#M" cause="additive">raka-raka</rdg>
3395</app>
. vovohan, pisaṅ kǝmbaṅ den asaṅkǝp, duvәgan, upacara dhūpā dīpa, vīja candanenasab,</ab>
.<ab>
.<app>
.<lem type="emn">sajiakәna</lem>
3400<rdg wit="#M #N">sajekna</rdg>
.</app>
. paraniṅ caru, riṅ bhaṭāra gaṅāpati, saṅ
.<app>
.<lem wit="#N">bhrәṅgiritī</lem>
3405<rdg wit="#M">bhr̥giriti</rdg>
.</app>,
. saṅ hyaṅ iśvarā, bhaṭārī umā, sira paḍa aturana caru,</ab>
.
. <ab>lumәkas kita
3410<app>
.<lem wit="#N">anambuta</lem>
.<rdg wit="#M">anambutana</rdg>
.</app>
. brata, maśucya radina śarīra, aṅabakti riṅ saṅgar,
3415 <abbr>ma,</abbr> om̐ nandīśvara mahākālaya namaḥ, om̐
.<app>
.<lem type="emn">bhrәṅgiriṭībhyaṃ</lem>
.<rdg wit="#M #N">bhrәṅgiritī</rdg>
.</app>
3420 namaḥ, om̐ sam̐ sāptarṣibhyo namaḥ, om̐ maheśvarāya namaḥ, om̐ śrī
.<app>
.<lem type="emn">umāyai</lem>
.<rdg wit="#M #N">umāye</rdg>
.</app>
3425 namaḥ, tәlas haturakǝn carunta riṅ deva, <abbr>ma,</abbr> om̐ im̐ namaḥ, om̐ deva carave namaḥ, amr̥tātmakāya svāhā.
. </ab>
.
. <ab xml:id="tattvabrata_66">yan alabvana brata kadi ṅūni, duk vahu lumәkasa brata, luvarana gәlaṅ lave kuniṅ, mahuvusana ri tilǝmiṅ bhadravāda juga.

3440<!-- G nihan paṅastutiniṅ brata, riṅ vulan āmr̥ttamaśa, kavruhakna, ḷkasnyā hamatighni, sarahina, yaniṅ vulan kaphaṭ, hamr̥ttamaśanya, riṅ pūrṇnama, mantra stutinira, yan aṅabakti åmvitiṅ saṅgar·, ma, om̐ tvaṣṭa vai devā mr̥tta tvam, porṇnamāsi namo stute, mamocya sarva papebhyā, candra ….{lo}kaṅ sagaccāti, saṅ hyaṅ ṅāsmara devatanya, bratanya ayva maṅan sarva rondon, phalanya dhadi śiṅ tinandhurtā. Caru sarva pavitra, tumpәṅ putih, papaṅgaṅ itik, graṅ grih, yantiga, sdhah vho, raka vo-vohan, pisaṅ kәmbaṅ, dhupa den asaṅkәp, mantraniṅ ṅhaṅaturakәñ caru, ma, om̐ devācara ve namaḥ, candra deva ya svāha||
.
.yaniṅ vulan, 5, riṅ tiḷm amr̥ttamaśanya, saṅ hyaṅ mahadeva devatanya, bratanya, ayva vuvus ala, ayva nәmbaṅ boñcah, phalanya, dr̥man āvәvәkasan. Caru tuṅgal kadi ṅuni, mantra stutinira, om̐ mitra vai devāmr̥tta tvaṅ, åpavasya damostute, mamocyā sarva papebhyā, åghnilokaṅ sagaccāti. Aturakna carunta riṅ deva kadi ṅuni, ma, om̐ devā cara ve nāmah, ådeva ya svāhā || yaniṅ vulan, 6, riṅ piṅ volu amr̥ttamaśanya, bratanya, tuṅgal kadi ṅuni, saṅ hyaṅ ṅatanu devatanya, bratanya yva ṅinәp, yan aluluṅā, phalanya sugih tan kahilaṅan, caru kadi ṅuni, mantra stutinya, om̐ kr̥ṣṇā ve devā mr̥tta tvaṅ, åṣṭamyantu namo stute, mamocyā sarva papebhyā, viṣṇu lokaṅ sagacchati. Åturākna caruntā kadi ṅuni, ma, om̐ devācara ve namaḥ, viṣṇu devā ya svāhā || yaniṅ kapitu, riṅ piṅ tiga vlas, amr̥ttamaśanya, bratanya tuṅgal kadi ṅūni, saṅ hyaṅ manasija devatanya, bratanya, åṅrakā, phalanya sugih kedhәp, kātkan siṅ sinadyanta, caru kadi ṅūni, mantra stutinira, om̐ bāruṇā devā mr̥tta tvaṅ, trayodaśya namostute, mamocya sarva papebhyā, rudrālokaṅ sagacchati. Åturakna carunta kadi ṅūni, ma, om̐ devācara ve nāmah, rūdrā devāta ya svāhā || yaniṅ vulan kavolu, piṅ ro åmr̥ttamāśanya, brata tuṅgal kadi ṅūni, saṅ hyaṅ anaṅga devatanya, bratanya, ayva maṅan suku paṭ, phalanya sugih patik vnaṅ, caru kadi ṅūni, mantra stutinira, om̐ vivāśvandevā mr̥tta tvaṅ, dvitiyaccha namo stute, mamocyā sarva pāpebhyā, sūryyālokaṅ sagacchati, aturakna carunta riṅ devā, ma, om̐ devā cara ye namaḥ, sūryyā devāta ya svāha || yaniṅ vulan kasaṅa, riṅ piṅ ṅәnәm amr̥ttamasanya, brata tuṅgal kadi ṅūni, saṅ hyaṅ ravi devatanya, ayva maṅan āsu, phalanya pәkik rāspati, polih prajurit, caru kadi ṅūni, mantra stutinira, om̐ åṅśah ve devā mr̥tta tvaṅ, ṣaṣtyāñceva nāmostute, mamoccha sarva papebhyā, årkkalokaṅ, sagacchati, åtūrakna taṅ caru riṅ devā, mantra, om̐ devācara ve namaḥ, årkkā devā ya svāha || yaniṅ vulan kaśapuluh, riṅ piṅ paṭ āmr̥ttamaśanya, saṅ hyaṅ brahmā devatanya, ayva ndәḷṅ ruhūr·, phalanya kinasihaniṅ hyaṅ, caru kadi ṅūni, māntra stutinira, om̐ dāta devā mr̥tvaṅ, catūrttyantu namo stute, mamocyā sarva papebhyā, brahmalokaṅ sagacchati, brata kadi ṅūni, haṅaturākna taṅ caru, ma, om̐ devācara ve nāmah, dhatr̥ devā ya nāmah svāhva || yaniṅ vulan jyeṣṭā, riṅ piṅ limā amr̥ttamāśanya, brata kadi ṅuni, saṅ hyaṅ ekājaya hyaṅnya, bratanya, ayva ñampat, phalanya, kedhep mandi kcāpta, caru kadi ṅuni, mantra stutinira, om̐ indra ve devāmr̥tta tvaṅ, pañcamyantu namo stute, mamocya sarva pāpebhyā, indralokaṅ sagacchati, atūrakna carunta, ma, om̐ devācara ve nāmah, indra devā ya svāhā || yaniṅ ṅulan sadha, riṅ pratipadha śuklā amr̥ttamaśanya, bratanya, tuṅgal kadi ṅuni, saṅ hyaṅ virāyoddha devatanya, bratanya, ayva turu lavan istrīnya, phalanya, ke……h omahta || caru kadi ṅuni, mantra stutinira, om̐ åryya madevā mr̥tta tvaṅ, pratipadha namo stute, mamocya sarva pāpebhyo, årkkalokaṅ sagacchati. Haturakna carunta, mantra, om̐ devācara ve namaḥ, årkkā devā ya svāhā || yaniṅ vulan kaśa, riṅ piṅ sapuluh amr̥ttamasanya, bratanya, tuṅgal kadi ṅūni, saṅ hyaṅ virakusuma devatanya, bratanya, ayva maṅan phala buṅkah, phalanya, sugih anom, dr̥man avәvәkasan, caru tuṅgal kadi ṅūni, mantra stutinira, om̐ bhāganah devāmr̥tta tvaṅ, daśamyantu namo stute, mamocyā sarva pāpebhyo, viśvalokaṅ sagacchati. Atūrakna caru, ma, om̐ devācara ve namaḥ, bhaga deva ya svāhā || yaniṅ vulan karo, riṅ piṅ pitu ama tka maśanya, bratanya kadi ṅūni, saṅ hyaṅ jaya kusuma devatanya, bratanya, ayva maṅan sapi, phalanya luputiṅ tuju tlu, dr̥man ātiven-iven, caru kadi ṅūni, mantra stutinira, om̐ puṣyā ve devā mr̥tta tvaṅ, saptāmyantu namostute, mamocyā sarva pāpebhyā, sūryyalokaṅ sagacchati. Aturakna carunta, om̐ devācara ve nāma, puṣya deva ya svāhā || yaniṅ vulan katiga, riṅ piṅ saṅa hamr̥ttamaśanya, brata kadi ṅuni, saṅ hyaṅ manobhāva devātanya, bratanya, ayva maṅan celeṅ, phalanya luputiṅ griṅ ṅāguṅ, caru kadi ṅuni, mantra stutinira, om̐ parjjādyah devā mr̥tta tvaṅ, nāvamyantu namostute, mamocyā sarva pāpebhyā, indralokaṅ sagacchati, hatūrakna ya caruntā, ma, om̐ devācara ve namaḥ, indra devā ya svāha ||0|| gnap ikaṅ brata samaṅkana, rva vlas vulan ri kalaniṅ kāhamr̥ttamaśanya, hamatighni, hiṅhanta phalanya, kapaṅguh denira saṅ maṅhanakәn brata, dirghyayuṣā paripūrṇna, riṅ dlāha maṅdadyakәn rātu viśeṣā, ayvā cavuh, yan kalaniṅ abrata ||0|| -->
.
.
3445
.
.
.<!-- G -->
.
3450<!-- M nihan tiṅkahiṅ ābrata ri mr̥tta maśa, ṅa, hal̥kasā kittha hamati ghni, samaptā rahinā, mvaṅ caru sarvva pavitra, tumpə̄ṅ putih, papaṅgaṅ Iṭik, graṅ grih hantigan, sdhah voh, rakā vovohan, pisaṅ kәmbaṅ dhūpa den asaṅkәp ||0|| nihan paṅvijiknya,

.
.<!-- U nihan tingkahiṅṅ abrata riṅṅ amrata māṣa, ṅa, haṅkәsakәn kita hāmati gni, samapṭā rahina, mvaṅ caru sarvva pavitra, tumpәṅ putih, papaṅgāṅaṅ itik graṅ grih hantiga, sdah voh rakā vovohan, pisaṅ kәmbāṅ, dhupa den asaṅkәp. nihan paṅuvijinya,
.
. yaniṅ vulan, ka, 4, pūrṇnama, stuti nira riṅ saṅgar·, ma, om̐ tvastace devā mr̥tattvam, pūrṇnama si namostute, mamoccya sarvva pāpebhyo, candra leka sagaścati. haturakna carunta kadi ṅuni, ma, om̐ deva caru ve namaḥ, candra deva ya svāhā.-->

.<!-- M gnәp tiṅkahiṅ brata samaṅkanā, rva vlas vulan kala niṅ hamr̥tta masa hamate ghni, kapaṅgih de saṅ haṅanakәn brata, dīrggha yuṣa, paripūrṇna, riṅ dlāha mandādi ratu viśeṣā, hayva cavuh yan kala niṅ habrata, tlas,
.
.sma ta brataṅkәna mravani siṅ pravani, Utamā dahat, tuhā gana ta ya bāratā, byakta tuṣṭātmakā saṅ piṭara nirā, tka riṅ kāki buyut īra suka, nītya sukātma ka vaneh, Ika ta den agatikna ddheniṅ amaṅunāyu niṅ śarirātma-->
.
4140<!-- N gnǝp tiṅkahiṅ brata samaṅkana, rva vlas vulan , kalaniṅ hamr̥tta maśa, Amati ghni, kapaṅgih de saṅ haṅanakǝn brata, dīrgghā yuṣa paripurṇna, riṅ dlāha, mandadi ratū viśeṣā, hayva cavuh yan kalaniṅ ābrattta, tlas,
.
.smā, tabrataṅkǝna mravani siṅ pravani, Uttamā dahat, tuhvā gana ta ya bharaṭā , byakta tuṣṭātmakā saṅ pitārannirā, tka rīṅ kaki buyutira suka, nītya sukātmaka vaneh, Ika ta den agatiniṅ amaṅun ayuniṅ śarīrātma-->
.
.<!-- P gәnәpniṅ tiṅkahniṅ brata, samaṅkana rva vәlas vulan kalaniṅ hamr̥ta maṣa, hamati gәnine saṅ haṅanakākәn brata, dirgha yuṣa paripūrṇna, ri dlahan mandadi ratu śakti maviśeṣa, hayva cavuh kālaniṅ yan habrata -->
4145
.<!-- U gnap tiṅkah iṅ brāta maṅkana, rva vlas vulan kāla niṅ amr̥ta māsa, hamāti gni, kapaṅgih de saṅ haṅanakәn brata, dirgghā yuṣa paripūrṇna, riṅ dlahan maṅdadi ratu viśeṣā, hayva cahuh yan kākāla niṅṅ abrata-->
.

.<note>G and P are quite different here. 4955
.
.<p n="3" xml:id="tattvabrata_70.3">
. <app><lem wit="#M #N #U">pūrṇamaniṅ</lem><rdg wit="#P" cause="line_omission"></rdg></app>
. katiga, saṅ hyaṅ madhu kusuma,
4960 <app><lem wit="#N #U">pinakāvak</lem><rdg wit="#M">pinakiṅ</rdg></app>

. <app><lem type="norm">lituhayu</lem><rdg wit="#M #N">listvayu</rdg><rdg wit="#U">listvā</rdg></app>

4965 vicakṣaṇa, sukha sugih.</p>

4970
.<!-- M pūrnnama niṅ ṅkapat, saṅ hyaṅ hasmara, pinaka laki niṅ hulun, hapkik prajurit vicakṣanā, puruṣa viśeṣā, prajñan ṣuka sugih jayeṅ śatru, hasih pinakeṅ hulun-->

.<!-- P pūrṇnamaniṅ kapat, saṅ hyaṅ smara pinaka lakiniṅ hulun, hapәkik śakti prajurit vicakṣaṇa, prajñan suka sugih, hasih riṅ pinakeṅ hulun-->
.<!-- U pūrṇnama niṅ kapāt, saṅ hyaṅ hasmara pinakā lakiniṅṅ hulun, hapkik prajurit vicaksaṇā, puruṣa viśeṣa, prajñan suka sugih jayeṅ śatru, hasih ri pinakeṅ hulun.-->
4975
.<p n="4" xml:id="tattvabrata_70.4">
.pūrṇamaniṅ kapat, saṅ hyaṅ asmara pinakalaki ni ṅhulun,

4980 <app><lem wit="#M #N #U">puruṣa viśeṣa</lem><rdg wit="#P"><gap reason="omitted"></gap></rdg></app>, prajñan sukha sugih
. <app><lem wit="#M #N #U">jayeṅ śatru</lem><rdg wit="#P"><gap reason="omitted"></gap></rdg></app>,
. asih pinakeṅhulun.</p>
.
.
4985
.
.<!-- M pūrṇnama niṅ kalimā, saṅ hyaṅ manobavā, pinaka hanak iṅhulun, panәṅgek lanaṅ, hapkik prajurit, hasih pinakeṅ hulun, -->
.<!-- N purṇnamaniṅ kalimā, saṅ hyaṅ manobhava, pinakā hanakiṅ hulun , panǝṅgǝk lanaṅ, hapkik prajurit hasih pinakeṅ hulun-->
.<!-- P pūrṇnamāniṅ kalimā saṅ hyaṅ manobhava pinakā hanak iṅhulun, panәṅkәk lanaṅ, hapәkik prajurit, hasih riṅ pinakeṅ hulun-->
4990<!-- U pūrṇnama niṅ kalimā, saṅ hyaṅ manobhāva, pinaka hanak iṅṅ hulun, panәṅgәk lanaṅ, hapkik prajurit, hasih pinakeṅṅ hulun.-->
.
.
.<p n="5" xml:id="tattvabrata_70.5">
.pūrṇamaniṅ kalima, saṅ hyaṅ manobhava,
4995 <app><lem type="emn">pinakasānak </lem><rdg wit="#M #N #P #U">pinakaanak</rdg></app>

. <app><lem wit="#M #N #U">pinakeṅ</lem><rdg wit="#P" cause="additive">asih pinakeṅ</rdg></app>hulun.</p>
.
.
5000
.
.

.
. -->
.
5010<p n="6" xml:id="tattvabrata_70.6">
.

. pinakeṅhulun.</p>
.
5020
.
.

5030
.<p n="7" xml:id="tattvabrata_70.7">

. <app><lem wit="#M #N">asih</lem><rdg wit="#P #U" cause="additive">asih ri</rdg></app>

.
.
.

.<!-- U pūrṇnama niṅ kavolu, saṅ hyaṅ kāma ratih, pinakā sānak iṅ hulun lanaṅ varuju, sukā sugih hasih ri pinakeṅṅ hulun.-->
.
.<p n="8" xml:id="tattvabrata_70.8">
5045 pūrṇamaniṅ kavolu, saṅ hyaṅ kāma ratih pinakasānak i ṅhulun lanaṅ vuruju, sukha sugih asih
. <app><lem wit="#M #N #U">ri</lem><rdg wit="#P">riṅ</rdg></app>
. pinakeṅhulun.</p>
.

5050
.
.
.
.

5060

5070
.

.<p n="11" xml:id="tattvabrata_70.11">
. pūrṇamaniṅ jyeṣṭā, saṅ hyaṅ kumara,

5105
.

.
5110<!-- N purṇnamaniṅ hasadḍā, saṅ hyaṅ komari, pinakā hanak vadon paṅguṅgulu, listvasyu paripurṇnā, ḍr̥man keḍǝp, puruṣa viśeṣā, prajñān vicakṣaṇā, hahiḍǝpinakeṅ hulun-->
.
.<!-- P pūrṇnamaniṅ hasaddha, saṅ hyaṅ komari pinakā hanak vadon paṅggulu, listuhayu, paripūrṇna dr̥man kedhәp , puruṣa viśeṣa, prajñan vicakṣaṇa hahidhәp pinakeṅ hulun-->

5115
.

.<p n="12" xml:id="tattvabrata_70.12">

.

.<p xml:id="tattvabrata_70.13">
. <app><lem wit="#M #N #U">phalani ṅhulun</lem><rdg wit="#P">phalaniṅ</rdg></app>
. aṅaji tutug, aṅavruhakǝn
5195 <app><lem wit="#M #N #P">anutug abapa, ababu, tutuga</lem><rdg wit="#U"><gap reason="omitted"></gap></rdg></app>
. malaky arabi,
. <app><lem wit="#P">maanak-anak</lem><rdg wit="#M #N #U">anak-anak</rdg></app>
. tutug asanak, tutug akaki anini, tutug aputu abuyut, tumus riṅ tǝmbe, abagus kalavan ayu, paripūrṇa, drәman
. <app><lem wit="#M #N #U">keḍәp</lem><rdg wit="#P">sahiḍәp</rdg></app>,
5200 sukha sugih, śrī sadana, mās maṇik, dodot
. <app><lem wit="#P">lәlәmes</lem><rdg wit="#M #N" cause="haplography">lәmǝs</rdg><rdg wit="#U">ulәmәs</rdg></app>,
. <app><lem wit="#M #N">akveh</lem><rdg wit="#P #U">kveh</rdg></app>
. <app><lem wit="#N #P">dasih</lem><rdg wit="#M">daśah</rdg><rdg wit="#U">dasi</rdg></app>,
. vәnaṅ-vәnaṅ asuku pat, asuku ro,
5205 <app><lem wit="#M #N">sugih tany akәna hiren</lem><rdg wit="#P">sugihanya kәna hiren</rdg><rdg>sugih tan kәna hiren</rdg></app>,
. siddha
. <app><lem wit="#U">saprayojana</lem><rdg wit="#M #N #P">saprayojñana</rdg></app>,
. siddha salampah salaku, lǝvih kapaṅgih
. <app><lem wit="#M #N #U">riṅ tǝmbe pañjanman</lem><rdg wit="#P">lәvih kapaṅgih maṅke</rdg></app>,
5210 lәvih
. <app><lem wit="#M #N #U">kapaṅgih maṅke</lem><rdg wit="#P" cause="transposition">kaṅ maṅko,
. tәmbe pañjanman</rdg></app>,
. bhagavan pañarikan anulisakǝn, saṅ hyaṅ triyodaśa sākṣi
. <app><lem wit="#M #N #U">anākṣeni</lem><rdg wit="#P">inakṣeni</rdg></app>,
5215 bhaṭāra hyaṅ kabayan añjǝnǝṅi.
.<app>
.<lem wit="#M #N #P #U"></lem>

.</p>

.

5230<!-- M nyan krama niṅ habrata riṅ śaśih, ka, 4, riṅ pradipadā śukla, caru śuci riṅ saṅgar·, sadan danan sovaṅ, riṅ sor pupulā, skar sataman, hnahakna ri har̥piṅ saṅ amūja, vus niṅ aṅabakti, tinirtthan, thar haṅupavaśa, sadinā saratri, Ikaṅ pupulā mvaṅ skar sataman, thәr vinaveṅ paturvan pinajaṅ pajaṅan, mne riṅ dhavuh ro, tka niṅ dhavuh, 7, haṅar̥pakna labahan sga pitā, hivak hiṭik ginoreṅ, saha sasahur·,-->

.
.<ab>yekiṅ mantra pralīna.</ab>
.<ab>om̐ śivāya śiva liṅgāya, śiva sarvomaheśvarah, <app><lem type="emn">namaḥ</lem><rdg wit="#N">nama</rdg></app> śivāya devāya, sadāśiva namo’stute.</ab>
.<ab>brahmā viṣṇviśvaro devāḥ, sarvajñā <app><lem type="norm">parameśvaraḥ</lem><rdg wit="#N">parameśvara</rdg></app>, utpatti sthiti linañ <app><lem type="emn">ca</lem><rdg wit="#N">cah</rdg></app>, liṅga deva namo namaḥ.</ab>
5380<ab>tuṅgal sthiti sārәpiṅ pralīna.</ab>
.
.<ab>yen harәp śīva rātri cǝṇdhǝk, liṅanta,</ab>
.<ab>om̐ om̐ liṅgā liṅgādipataye namaḥ, om̐ om̐ atma liṅgāya namaḥ,
.sǝmbah duk sore, om̐ om̐ paramaśiva liṅgāya namaḥ,
5385sǝmbah tәṅah vәṅi, om̐ om̐ śūnya liṅgāya namaḥ,
.sǝmbah meh rahina, sәminiṅ maja pinūjākǝn, sthuti tuṅgal, om̐ nama śivāya, namo rudrāya, <app><lem type="emn">niśāḍha</lem><rdg wit="#N">nispada</rdg></app> <app><lem type="emn">parvata sthāya</lem></app>, <supplied reason="omitted">liṅggādhipatir adhipati svāhā</supplied>saha sǝmbah sәminiṅ maja kunaṅ.</ab>
.
.<ab xml:id="tattvabrata_72">lviriṅ
.<app><lem type="norm">brata hayva kәna</lem><rdg wit="#N">bratayvakәna</rdg></app>
5390riṅ tamah, tamah harane turu, yatika kavaśakәna <app><lem type="emn">hayva</lem><rdg wit="#N">yva</rdg></app> lupa, i kālanta mabrata, hayva juga kita aturu ri rahina, hila-hila, hilaṅ ulihta mabrata, asiṅ brata anisphala tan pantuka asiṅ sinadya, mataṅnyan kayatnakәna, hayva iman-iman, ikaṅ tapa brata agәṅ phalanya, vāhya sukha katәmu donya, ikaṅ kayogiśvaran, kamokṣan phalanya, mataṅnyan hayva cumacadiṅ sira saṅ lumәkasakǝn brata tapa, hayva memeṅen iṅ vvaṅ abrata, hila-hila liṅ saṅ hyaṅ.
.</ab>
.</div>
.
.<!-- G … jala pravira subirāt, sugih tan pamaṅun gave, muvah akaravaṅan, habaṅ rūpanira,[41v] sar̥ṅit gәṅira, ya hiku sariniṅ galuṅan, pinakasamtoniṅ ulun, siṅ tan vruh sariniṅ galuṅan, pinakakavudhanan ūlun sa….gat, saravanā, satuṅkәbiṅ rat, siṅ haṅavruhi sāriniṅ ṅgāluṅan, ya pinakasa{na}k iṅulun, pinaka{ka}dhaṅiṅ hulun, sasaṅoniṅ hulun āṅavruhakan sāriniṅ ṅgāluṅan, salave lakṣa, salave kṭi, salave yuta, salave barā, salave hiṅәl, pinakapasasaṅoniṅ ṅhulun, katmu samaṅko katmu tambe, ḷvih maṅko ḷvih tәmbe, mtu salakṣā sadina. om̐ I A om̐, sa…-->

. jaya pravira subiṅ rāt, sugih tan pamaṅun gave, muvah hakaravaṅan , habaṅ rūpanira, sār̥ṅit gə̄ṅira, ya hiku sariniṅ galuṅan , pinakāsamtoniṅ hulun , siṅ tan vruh sariniṅ galuṅan , pinakā kavulaniṅ hulun , sabhūvana, satuṅkǝbiṅ rāt, siṅ haṅavruhi sariniṅ galuṅān , ya pinaka sanakiṅ hulun, pinakā samtoniṅ hulun , sasaṅoniṅ hulun , haṅavruhākǝn sarīniṅ galuṅan , salave lākṣa, salave kṭi, salave hiṅǝl, pinakā pasasaṅoniṅ hulun , katmu maṅko, katmu tǝmbe, lǝvih kātmu tǝmbe, mtu salākṣa sadinā, om̐ sa ba ta A I, nama śiva ya, A U ma om̐ -->
.
.

.

. pinakasānakiṅ hulun,

.<ab xml:id="tattvabrata_147">hana brata, maṅan amona, tan paṅinum bañu, vusiṅ amaṅan aṅinum bañu, aṅūcapakәna, <abbr>pha</abbr>, tan kәna

7145 viśeṣa riṅ bhūmi, keḍәp kapintuhu, pituṅ śaśih divasanya.

.
7150
.

.<div type="subchapter" n="3.148">
.<ab xml:id="tattvabrata_148">hana brata, monāraka, tan paṅucap lamun amaṅan, tәluṅ tahun samayanya, bhaṭāra rudra hyaṅniṅ brata,
7155 <abbr>pha</abbr>,

.<div type="subchapter" n="3.149">
.<ab xml:id="tattvabrata_149">hana brata,
7165 mona maṅan. mona nap. mona muris. mona susur<supplied reason="omitted">.</supplied> mona bhasma. mona napuh. mona ṅisiṅ.</ab>
.
.<p xml:id="tattvabrata_149.0">kunaṅ mulihiṅ mona,</p>
.
.<p n="1" xml:id="tattvabrata_149.1"> mona maṅan, <abbr>pha</abbr>, vicakṣaṇa dīrgha yuṣa kita.</p>
7170
.<p n="2" xml:id="tattvabrata_149.2"> mona nap, <abbr>pha</abbr>, kinasihan deniṅ rāt, prabhu viku.</p>
.
.<p n="3" xml:id="tattvabrata_149.3"> mona bhasma, <abbr>pha</abbr>, mantuk iṅ bhaṭārī rātri, sasarnya majanma riṅ viku śakti.</p>
.
7175<p n="4" xml:id="tattvabrata_149.4"> mona napuh, <abbr>pha</abbr>, kinasihaniṅ paṇḍita, mvaṅ deva prabhu, rahayu riṅ pañjanmanta.</p>
.
.<p n="5" xml:id="tattvabrata_149.5"> mona ṅisiṅ, <abbr>pha</abbr>, prih meṅgal katәmu, bahusiṣya kita.</p>
.
.<p n="6" xml:id="tattvabrata_149.6"> mona sisig, <abbr>pha</abbr>, jaya kāryanta, prabha kiteṅ kamokṣan.</p>
7180
.<p n="7" xml:id="tattvabrata_149.7"> mona muris, <abbr>pha</abbr>, siddhakāryanta, pinrihta muna təka.</p>
.</div>
.
.
7185
.
.

.<ab xml:id="tattvabrata_170">hana brata, maṅan tumpǝṅ
. <app><lem type="emn">mevak</lem><rdg wit="#N">ivak</rdg></app> uyah harәṅ, bhaṭāra iśvara hyaṅnya, ya pinakarūpa, pinakaśvaraniṅ kiduṅ carita,
7535 <abbr>pha</abbr>, manisiṅ panutukan.
. <app><lem wit="#N #P"></lem>
. <note> hana brata, maṅan ... manisiṅ panutukan <note>
. </note>
. <ptr target="#N"/> in III.171 <ptr target="#P"/> quite similiar, but different in the technique and the result. Here is the P: hana brata maṅan tumpәṅ ivaknya huyah harәṅ, pәtaṅ tavun samayanya, kinasihan deniṅ padhanta janma </note>
7540</app>
.</ab>
.</div>
.
.
7545
.
.<div type="subchapter" n="3.171">
.<ab xml:id="tattvabrata_171">hana brata, amaṅan kǝmbaṅ, naṅkǝn,
. <abbr>u</abbr>,
7550 <app><lem type="emn">mevak</lem><rdg wit="#N">ivak</rdg></app>
. uyah harәṅ, vusiṅ amaṅan, aṅinaṅ suruh pupucuk, aṅliṅga kǝmbaṅ,
. <abbr>ṅa</abbr>,
. <abbr>pha</abbr>,
. sukha sugih, rūpa aheṅ.
7555</ab>
.</div>
.
.
.
7560<div type="subchapter" n="3.172">
.<ab xml:id="tattvabrata_172">hana brata, amaṅan tan pauyah, pituṅ vәṅi samayanya,
. <abbr>pha</abbr>,
. śaktinta ḍatәṅ, tәhәr kinatvaṅan deniṅ hyaṅ. </ab>
.</div>
7565
.
.
.<div type="subchapter" n="3.173">
.<ab xml:id="tattvabrata_173">hana brata, amaṅan
7570 arasotih,
. <abbr>ṅa</abbr>, aḍahar uyah harәṅ
. <app><lem type="norm">pinakavulam</lem><rdg wit="#N">minakavulam</rdg></app>,
. lama pituṅ dina, ra nini paduka bhaṭārī
. <app><lem type="norm">sarasvatī</lem><rdg wit="#N">śarasoti</rdg></app>
7575 hyaṅniṅ brata,
. <abbr>pha</abbr>, prajñan.
.</ab>
.</div>
.
7580
.<div type="subchapter" n="3.174">
.<ab xml:id="tattvabrata_174">nihan kr̥ta māsa,
. <abbr>ṅa</abbr>,
. hayuniṅ hulun,
7585 <app><lem type="emn">akārya</lem><rdg wit="#N">sakārya</rdg></app>
. hayu, makādi vatǝk abrata, nūt avarah,</ab>
.
.<p n="1" xml:id="tattvabrata_174.1">śaśih ka, 1, taṅ, piṅ, 10, saṅ hyaṅ vīra kusuma devatanya, bratanya, hayva maṅan sarvabuṅkah,
. <abbr>pha</abbr>, sugih anom
7590 drәman avǝvәka ta sira.</p>
.
.<p n="2" xml:id="tattvabrata_174.2">śaśih, 2, taṅ, piṅ, 7, saṅ hyaṅ jaya kusuma devatanya, bratanya hayva maṅan sapi,
. <abbr>pha</abbr>, luputeṅ tuju tәluh tarañjana, drәman ahiven iven.</p>
.
7595<p n="3" xml:id="tattvabrata_174.3"> śaśih, 3, taṅ, piṅ, 9, saṅ hyaṅ naka devatanya, bratanya, hayva maṅan bavi,
. <abbr>pha</abbr>, tan katampǝkan gәriṅ aguṅ.</p>
.
.<p n="4" xml:id="tattvabrata_174.4">śaśih, 4, taṅ, piṅ, 15, saṅ hyaṅ asmara devatanya, bratanya, hayva maṅan sarvaroṇḍon,
. <abbr>pha</abbr>,
7600 dadi siṅ tinandur.</p>
.
.<p n="5" xml:id="tattvabrata_174.5">śaśih, 5, paṅloṅ, piṅ, 15, saṅ hyaṅ mahādeva devatanya, bratanya, hayva sǝhǝk yan aṅucap, hayva <app><lem type="emn">ṅǝmban</lem><rdg wit="#N">nǝṅbaṅ</rdg></app>
. boñcah,
. <abbr>pha</abbr>, drәman avǝvәka.</p>
7605
.<p n="6" xml:id="tattvabrata_174.6">śaśih, 6, taṅ, piṅ, 8, saṅ hyaṅ atanu devatanya, bratanya, hayva aṅinǝp, riṅ paluluṅhān,
. <abbr>pha</abbr>,
. sugih tan kelaṅ elaṅan.</p>
.
7610<p n="7" xml:id="tattvabrata_174.7">śaśih, 7, taṅ, piṅ, 13, saṅ hyaṅ manasija devatanya, bratanya, aṅraka,
. <abbr>pha</abbr>,
. sugih keḍәp kapaṅgih siṅ giṇa harṣa.</p>
.
.<p n="8" xml:id="tattvabrata_174.8">śaśih, 8, taṅ, piṅ, 2, saṅ hyaṅ anaṅgara devatanya, bratanya, hayva amaṅan paṭik vǝnaṅ suku pat,
7615 <abbr>pha</abbr>, sugih patik vǝnaṅ.</p>
.
.<p n="9" xml:id="tattvabrata_174.9">śaśih, 9, taṅ, piṅ, 6, saṅ hyaṅ ravi devatanya, bratanya, hayva maṅan asu,
. <abbr>pha</abbr>,
. apәkik raspati prajurit.</p>
7620
.<p n="10" xml:id="tattvabrata_174.10">śaśih, 10, taṅ, piṅ, 4, saṅ hyaṅ brahmā devatanya, bratanya, hayva maṅan andǝlәṅ riṅ luhur, <abbr>pha</abbr>, kinasihaniṅ hyaṅ, mvaṅ voṅ mule
. <app><lem type="norm">akveh</lem><rdg wit="#N">akeh</rdg></app>
. asih iri kita.</p>
.
7625<p n="11" xml:id="tattvabrata_174.11">śaśih, jyeṣṭa, taṅ, piṅ, 5, saṅ hyaṅ leka jaya devatanya, bratanya, aṅlampar ananapu,
. <abbr>pha</abbr>, keḍәp mandi sakәcapta.</p>
.
.<p n="12" xml:id="tattvabrata_174.12">śaśih, saddhā, taṅ, piṅ, 1, saṅ hyaṅ pisodharī devatanya, bratanya, hayva turu lavan
. <app><lem type="norm">strī</lem><rdg wit="#N">istri</rdg></app>, <abbr>pha</abbr>,
7630 keḍәp aomah-omah.</p>
.
.<p xml:id="tattvabrata_174.13">iya ṅitaṅ kariṅ vulan, kr̥ta masa haranya, den asthiti sira, keṅәtakәna
. <app><lem type="norm">hayva</lem><rdg wit="#N">yva</rdg></app> lupa.</p>
.</div>
7635
.
.
.<div type="subchapter" n="3.175">
.<ab>hana brata, saninigraha,
7640 <abbr>ṅa</abbr>,
. tan mamati aghni ri kālaniṅ tumpǝk kalivon<supplied reason="omitted">,</supplied>
. <app><lem type="emn">molaha</lem><rdg wit="#N">moliha</rdg></app>
. sapuluh tumpәk kalivon,
. kramanya
7645 <app><lem type="emn">amuja</lem><rdg wit="#P">tamumuja</rdg></app>,
. ananapuh eṅ saṅgar,
. <app><lem type="emn">amvit</lem><rdg wit="#N">tāmvit</rdg></app>
. anǝmbaha ri bhaṭāra śīvāditya, lviriṅ caru riṅ saṅgar, anapunar, arih, rәmbaṅ, tambo lagu akah araka, phala, kambaṅ vaṅi, burat vaṅi, lәṅa vaṅi, sәḍǝṅan ikṣu, dīpa, dhūpa, den asaṅkǝp, devadarv inasab, vīja, dhūpa, ika kahatur i bhaṭāra,
. <abbr>ma</abbr>,
7650 om̐ namo bhagavatye vaśūdevāya, sarvatuṣṭan, dadāsime, om̐ śrī gurubhyo namaḥ, devacarundādasi mahātrәpti svāhā.</ab>
.
. <ab xml:id="tattvabrata_175">tәlas ta ṅavaṅia ta kita,
. <abbr>ma</abbr>,
. om̐ sūrya putrāya namaḥ.
7655 samaṅkana taṅ brata lәkasakәna, hayva ta pramada riṅ brata, kunaṅ yan kālaṅan agriṅ, sakalviraniṅ aṅalaṅana, pinakavuruṅaniṅ brata, hayva pinakṣakǝn ikaṅ brata, kaliṅanya mvitana juga muvah, kunaṅ yan tan kalaṅana, anulus rahayu, pakṣakәna ika,
. <abbr>pha</abbr>,
. riṅ dlāhanta dadi ratu sukha vāhya katәmu, pinakāśraya deniṅ paḍanta ratu, keḍәp kapintuhu deniṅ rāt kabeh.</ab>
.</div>
.
7660
.
.<div type="subchapter" n="3.176">
.<ab xml:id="tattvabrata_176">iti
. <app><lem type="conj">sāriniṅ</lem><rdg wit="#N" cause="haplography">sani</rdg></app>
7665 brata, kayatnakәna de saṅ
. <app><lem type="emn">amet</lem><rdg wit="#N">met</rdg></app>
. hayu, ndan ika hayva malәtuh ikaṅ ambǝk, mataṅyan ika hayva
. <app><lem type="emn">mithya</lem><rdg wit="#N">miṣya</rdg></app> buddhi, tātkalanta maṅanakǝn brata, apan yan tan karakṣa ikaṅ brata denta, maṅdadyakǝn vighnaniṅ śarīra, yan enak denta rumakṣa sarīra, makajñāna buddhi mahottama, malilaṅa ahniṅ nirāvaraṇa, tan
. <app><lem type="emn">pagәlәh-gәlәh</lem><rdg wit="#N">pagәlә-gәlәh</rdg></app>,
7670 tan karakәtan karṇa śūla, mvaṅ rajah tamah, ika ta maṅdadyakǝn svarga magәṅ, ṅuniveh jñāna viśeṣa, vruha ri kramanira sovaṅ-sovaṅ.
.</ab>
.</div>
.
.<div type="subchapter" n="3.177">
7675<ab xml:id="tattvabrata_177">hana brata sabran
. <app><lem type="emn">umanis</lem><rdg wit="#N">manis</rdg></app>,
. <abbr>ṅa</abbr>,
. tan pamaṅan tampakiṅ apuy, rvaṅ vulan samayanya,
.sabran pahiṅ tan pamaṅan tampakiṅ aghni, rvaṅ vulan samayanya,
7680sabran pon tan padus tan palәṅa, tan pararavup, tan pakәkәmuh, rvaṅ vulan samayanya,
.sabran vage, tan paturu gumuliṅ, rvaṅ vulan samayanya,
.sabran kalivon, tan paṅucap-ucap, rvaṅ vulan samayanya,
.<abbr>pha</abbr>,
. ginañjar deniṅ vatǝk devata kabeh, norana nūkr̥tani, tan hilaṅ takonakәna, drәventa tǝmbe.
7685
.</ab>
.</div>
.
.<div type="subchapter" n="3.178">
7690<ab xml:id="tattvabrata_178">nihan haji pabrata, yaniṅ taṅgal piṅ lima, anuju kalivon, paṅupavāśa,</ab>
.<p n="1" xml:id="tattvabrata_178.1"> esuknya riṅ
. <app><lem type="norm">umanis</lem><rdg wit="#N">manis</rdg></app>, amaṅan kupat pāṇḍava, 5, ivaknya kacaṅ,
. <abbr>pha</abbr>,
. dukiṅ alit duruṅ anәmu, yan vus agәṅ amaṅgih sukha sugih aguṅ dunya.</p>
7695
.<p n="2" xml:id="tattvabrata_178.2"><abbr>pa</abbr>,
. amaṅan kupat syaṅ anti, 9, ivaknya komak,
. <abbr>pha</abbr>, tinuṅgu deniṅ rāma reṇa, aṅantos aputu abuyut, kinadhama deniṅ bapebu,
. <app><lem type="emn">kapti deniṅ</lem><rdg wit="#N">kaptini</rdg></app> hulun.</p>
7700
.<p n="3" xml:id="tattvabrata_178.3"><abbr>pva</abbr>,
. amaṅan kupat sidayu, 7, ivaknya sudhaṅ,
. <abbr>pha</abbr>, aṅapti listvayu, alit arampiṅ aṅlәlǝnte, tan amadhani, sukha sugih drәman baṅkit, pinarәkan pinakapahulunaniṅ maru. </p>
.
7705<p n="4" xml:id="tattvabrata_178.4"> <abbr>va</abbr>,
. amaṅan kupat sih tan pәgat, 4, ivaknya taluh,
. <abbr>pha</abbr>, aṅapti sukha sugih, drәman siddhi baṅkit, keḍәpiṅ alaki, tan kavaśa lakinta aṅluṅani, pinūji deniṅ matva, tanana ṅesǝm.</p>
.
.<p n="5" xml:id="tattvabrata_178.5"> <abbr>ka</abbr>,
7710 anәḍa kupat gәnǝp, 8, ivaknya raraśmen,
. <abbr>pha,</abbr>
. aṅapti sukha sugih aguṅ vīrya, añjǝnǝṅ arddha nareśvarī, keḍәp aṅucap.
. </p>
.<p n="6" xml:id="tattvabrata_178.6"> esuk riṅ
7715 <app><lem type="norm">umanis</lem><rdg wit="#N">manis</rdg></app>,
. anәḍa kupat siddha luṅguh, 10, ivaknya dagiṅ loh, sāgara dhanu, alas savah, dagiṅ pomahan,
. <supplied reason="omitted">pha,</supplied>
. aṅapti sukha sugih aguṅ vīrya, kinajrihan deniṅ śatru, kinadama deniṅ bala mvaṅ varga, pinarәkan deniṅ bala
. <app><lem type="norm">sabraṅ</lem><rdg wit="#N">sabran</rdg></app>,
7720 tan
. <app><lem type="emn">kevaṅan</lem><rdg wit="#N">ivaṅ</rdg></app>
. deniṅ bala, sami vatra tan anaṅsal, siddhi maṇḍi tan paṅucap, rәmrәm ikaṅ vvaṅ kabeh, riṅ panaṅkilan, tinaṅkiliṅ bala sakiṅ doh, abahan təka sakiṅ tan hana, sabran-sabran, yan vadon sinivi deniṅ maru, tan hana maḍani, sadera ṅrehakәna, vr̥ddhi putra, kinajrihan deniṅ santana, vīrya bhukti, embuh mañabuh, imbuh-imbuh tan paṅloṅ. sami danur daha.
.</p>
.</div>
7725
.
.<!-- G hana brāta nuṅkurat, ṅa, kalivon hama, manis amadhuhara, pahiṅ habāyu hara, pvan atoya hara, vage haghnihara, pūrṇnama tiḷm hamatihara, piṅ rvana kabeh Ika, hakabeh phalanya, hamupiṅ brata kabeh -->
.<!-- N hana brata nuṅku rāt, ṅa, kā, handumā. U, hamaḍūharā, pva, hambayuhāra, pva, hatoyahara, va, haghnihāra, purṇnamā, tīl̥m, hamatihāra,piṅ rvanakā, ṅa, pha, hamupusi brata kabeh -->
.<!-- U hana brata nuṅkurāt, ṅa, kalivon duma. manis hamadhuhāra. pahiṅ hambāyuhāra. pvan hatoyahara. vage hagnihāra. purṇnama til̥m hamatihāra. piṅ rva nikā, ṅa, Ikā ta kabeh, pha, hamuvusi brata kabeh -->
7730
.<div type="subchapter" n="3.179">
.<ab xml:id="tattvabrata_179">hana brata nuṅku rāt,
. <abbr>ṅa</abbr>,
. <app><lem wit="#G #U">kalivon</lem><rdg wit="#N">ka</rdg></app>
7735 <app><lem wit="#N">andhūma</lem><rdg wit="#G">hama</rdg><rdg wit="#U">duma</rdg></app>.
. <app><lem type="norm">umanis</lem><rdg wit="#G #U">manis</rdg><rdg wit="#N">U</rdg></app>,
. <app><lem type="norm">madhuāhāra</lem><rdg wit="#G #N #U">madhuhara</rdg></app>,
. <app><lem wit="#G #U">pahiṅ</lem><rdg wit="#N">pva</rdg></app>,
. <app><lem type="norm">abhāyuāhāra</lem><rdg wit="#G">abhayuhara</rdg><rdg wit="#N #U">ambhayuhara</rdg></app>,
7740 <app><lem wit="#G #U">pvan</lem><rdg wit="#N">pva</rdg></app>,
. <app><lem type="norm">atoyāhāra</lem><rdg wit="#G #N #U">atoyahara</rdg></app>,
. <app><lem wit="#G #U">vage</lem><rdg wit="#N">va</rdg></app>,
. <app><lem type="norm">aghniāhāra</lem><rdg wit="#G #N #U">aghnihāra</rdg></app>, pūrṇama, tīlәm,
. <app><lem type="norm">amatiāhāra</lem><rdg wit="#G #N #U">amatihāra</rdg></app>,
7745 <app><lem wit="#G">piṅ rvana kabeh</lem><rdg wit="#N">piṅrvanaka, ṅa</rdg><rdg wit="#U">piṅ rva nika</rdg></app>,
. <app><lem wit="#G"><abbr>pha</abbr></lem><rdg wit="#G">akabeh phalanya</rdg><rdg wit="#U">ika ta kabeh, pha,</rdg></app>, <app><lem wit="#N">amupusi brata kabeh</lem><rdg wit="#G">amupiṅ brata kabeh</rdg><rdg wit="#U">amuvusi brata kabeh</rdg></app>.
.
.<app><lem wit= "#G #N #U"></lem>
.<note> hana brata nuṅku ... brata kabeh <note>
7750</note>
.<ptr target="#G"/> in III.56 <ptr target="#N"/> in III.179 <ptr target="#U"/> in III.64 </note>
.</app>
.
.</ab>
7755</div>
.
.
.<!-- N hana brata, mañcadara, ṅa, manis amaṅan sga putih, pahiṅ hamāṅan ktan bāṅ, pvan hamaṅān sga kuniṅ, vage amaṅan ktan īr̥ṅ, kalivon amaṅan ktan hamañca vārṇna||0|| vetan amaṅan hantǝlu putihnya, kidul surā, kulon hantǝlu kuniṅ, lor bakakul, riṅ tṅah śarasi bāṅ hāti, pha, suka sugih-->
.
7760<!-- U hana brata mañca vara, ṅa, manis humaṅan sgā putih, pahiṅ amaṅan laktan bāṅ, pon amaṅan sgā kuniṅ, vage amaṅan ktan hir̥ṅ, kalivon, amaṅan ktan amañca varṇna, ṅa, vetan amaṅan sgā putih mvah Āntәlu putihnya, kidul sura, kulon hantalu kuniṅnya, lor bakatul, riṅ tṅah sarasi bāṅ hatih, pha, suka sugih -->
.
.
.<div type="subchapter" n="3.180">
.<ab xml:id="tattvabrata_180">hana brata,
7765 <app><lem wit="#U">mañcavāra</lem><rdg wit="#N">mañcadara</rdg></app>,
. <abbr>ṅa</abbr>,
. <app><lem type="norm">umanis</lem><rdg wit="#N #U">manis</rdg></app>
. <app><lem wit="#N">amaṅan</lem><rdg wit="#U">umaṅan</rdg></app>
. sәga putih, pahiṅ amaṅan
7770 <app><lem wit="#N">kәtan</lem><rdg wit="#U">lakәtan</rdg></app>
. baṅ,
. <app><lem wit="#U">pon</lem><rdg wit="#N">pvan</rdg></app>
. amaṅan sәga kuniṅ, vage amaṅan kәtan irәṅ, kalivon amaṅan kәtan amañca varṇa.
. vetan amaṅan
7775 <app><lem wit="#N">antǝlu putihnya</lem><rdg wit="#U">sәga putih mvah antәlu putihnya</rdg></app>, kidul sura, kulon antǝlu
. <app><lem wit="#N">kuniṅ</lem><rdg wit="#U">kuniṅnya</rdg></app>,
. lor
. <app><lem wit="#N">bakakul</lem><rdg wit="#U">bakatul</rdg></app>,
. riṅ tәṅah śarasi baṅ
7780 <app><lem wit="#N">hati</lem><rdg wit="#U">atih</rdg></app>,
. <abbr>pha</abbr>,
. sukha sugih.
. <app><lem wit="#N #U"></lem>
. <note> hana brata, mañcavara ... sukha sugih <note>
7785 </note>
. <ptr target="#N"/> in III.180 <ptr target="#U"/> in III.80 </note>
.</app>
.</ab>
.</div>
7790
.
.
.<div type="subchapter" n="3.181">
.<ab xml:id="tattvabrata_181">hana brata, anūt saptavāra,
7795 <abbr>ṅa</abbr>,
. <abbr>ra</abbr>, asisirih, 5,
. <abbr>ra</abbr>.
. <abbr>ca</abbr>, asisirih, 4,
. <abbr>ca</abbr>.
7800 <abbr>a</abbr>, asisirih, 3,
. <abbr>a</abbr>.
. <abbr>bu</abbr>, asisirih, 7,
. <abbr>bu</abbr>.
. <abbr>vrә</abbr>, asisirih, 8,
7805 <abbr>vrә</abbr>.
. <abbr>śu</abbr>, asisirih, 6,
. <abbr>śu</abbr>.
. <abbr>śa</abbr>, asisirih, 9,
. <abbr>śa</abbr>.
7810 <abbr>pha</abbr>,
. sukha sugih, vәnaṅ sakāma-kāma.
.</ab>
.</div>
.
7815<div type="subchapter" n="3.182">
.<ab xml:id="tattvabrata_182">hana brata, amaṅan sәkul
. <app><lem type="conj">slaṅgi</lem><rdg wit="#N">aṅgi</rdg></app>
. sarahup, sinaṅga ri taṅan kiva, tan patәḍa tan patambǝh, tigaṅ vәṅi samayanya, saṅ hyaṅ siddhi rakṣa sira turun abrata, uṅgvanira riṅ rāt,
. <abbr>pha</abbr>,
7820 tәḍunaniṅ drәman agave hayu, tan kapәjahan vәka kita, tәrus tumus tәkeṅ vәka vetbet.
.</ab>
.</div>
.
.
7825
.<div type="subchapter" n="3.183">
.<ab xml:id="tattvabrata_183">hana brata, maṅan sәkul saravup, sinaṅga ri taṅan kiva, tan patәḍa tan patambǝh,
. <supplied reason="omitted">ivaknya</supplied>
. lalab kevala, 3, vәṅi lavasnya, kārya hana putra,

9070 <abbr>pha</abbr><supplied reason="omitted">,</supplied> bisa ṅiduṅ, abәcikiṅ ulon, manisiṅ panutukan, mvaṅ kinasihaniṅ voṅ.

.
.
9075
.
.

.<ab xml:id="tattvabrata_290">[nyan ta saṅ citta varaṇā, umarah
