9625<ab>saṅ vala kula, mūla tattvaniṅ dadi kabeh, pahenak paṅrәṅə̄nta, mūlabhoktaniṅ kanirāśrayan, mvaṅ kābhyudayan, bhāvanya mvaṅ lakṣaṇanya, pūrvanya mvaṅ vәkasnya, maṅkana liṅ saṅ vala kula, nǝmbah hulun, om̐ viku satakvan tānaku, kita pva śikṣā ṅaran ika, duga-duga tumakvan, vuvus maṅkana, rәṅə̄n siptani ṅhulun.</ab>
.<ab>
.<foreign>pūrvaṃ śrī puruṣānte, varānugraha makanya, saṅ rojyam, narāsakane, ayavaṃ vidyāṃ prajayaṃ.</foreign>

9630<ab>
.maṅkana pariñciniṅ cipta, kaliṅanya, pūrva haraniṅ mimitan, tripuruṣa haraniṅ brahmā viṣṇu īśvara, vara ṅaraniṅ amidhi, anugraha haraniṅ panuṅsuṅ, manoka ṅaraniṅ devata, saroja ṅaraniṅ manūtra, nara ṅaraniṅ mānuṣa, sakāla ṅaraniṅ samaṅke, yaśa ṅaraniṅ kirti, vidyā ṅaraniṅ aji, aprayadha ṅaraniṅ pūjā,
.</ab>
.
.<ab>
9635kaliṅanya, bhaṭāra sira magave pratapa riṅ vana giri, maṅaṣkāra bhaṭāra, bhaṭārī, atitah kasukhan amragat trәṣṇa, anusupi vanavāsa, maṅǝnakǝn tapa, manaṅsāra rāga, tinūt deniṅ manūṣa maṅke, atapa abrata, ayoga asamadhī, ayajña dāna kīrti,
.</ab>
.
.<ab>
.maṅhanakǝn brata apayapanya, ulandriya, rumәgǝp pañcendriya, tuṅgalakәna riṅ trisandhyā, piṇdhakǝn riṅ kaparāmarthan, vaḍahana yoga, sahabana samadhi, tindihana brata, tuṅgunǝniṅ dāna kīrti, laṅlaṅana riṅ āgama, pagǝrana pupūjān sasapon, lavaṅana saṅgarma, ugǝr-ugǝrana sadā, inǝbana tuhu, tindihana kañciṅana parāmartha,
9640</ab>
.
.<ab>

.</ab>
9645
.<ab>

.<div type="translation">
10395
.<p corresp="#tattvabrata_00"> Om̐. Let there be no obstacle.</p>
.
.<p corresp="#tattvabrata_01">This is the <foreign>Right Behaviour</foreign>
. <note>According to the context of this passage, which explains the right behaviour when performing an observance, such as asking permission from the one who in charge in observance, offering betel leaves and reciting mantras, I have chosen <foreign>parikramaning</foreign> ‘proper order of things, right behaviour, customs (ritual) sanctioned by tradition’ (OJED, s.v.), as attested in mss. N and M. This is instead of <foreign>panarima</foreign>, probably a non-standard form of <foreign>panariman</foreign> ‘he who is given st., recipient’ (OJED, s.v.) as attested in mss. G and P, or <foreign>tiṅkahiṅ panarima</foreign>, meaning ‘way of acting for the recipient’ (the meaning of the word <foreign>tiṅkah</foreign> in OJED s.v.) as attested in ms. U. The words <foreign>parikrama</foreign>, <foreign>panarima</foreign> and <foreign>tiṅkahiṅ panarima</foreign> in Old Javanese have similar meanings. In the context of observance, the word <foreign>parikramaniṅ brata</foreign> emphasises the process of systematic conduct when performing the observance. Conversely, the word <foreign>panarima brata</foreign> and <foreign>tiṅkahiṅ panarima brata</foreign> emphasises the preparation of the practitioner before performing the observance.</note>
10400
. <foreign>in [Performing] Observances</foreign>. When you perform an observance, do not do it haphazardly, without having permission to the one who is in charge of the observances, [namely] the reverend Kaki<note>The word <foreign>kaki</foreign> means ‘grandfather; old man, elder; venerable’ (OJED, s.v.).</note> Citragopta<note>Citragopta or Citragupta is the keeper of the records of the good and evil deeds of human beings for Yama, and as such is well-known both from Skt. and OJ. literature (his name is also given as Citragotra. In Balinese tradition, he has a famous name as Saṅ Surātma). In <foreign>Kakavin Śivarātrikalpa</foreign> as already mentioned by Teeuw et al. (1969: 52) he reads a book with full account of one’s deed during one’s life. In India the book is called <foreign>Agrasandhāni</foreign>; in the <foreign>Kakavin Śivarātrikalpa</foreign> it is called a <foreign>galih</foreign>, but no specific name is given. </note> [and] Nini<note>The word <foreign>nini</foreign> means ‘grandmother; woman (used in designating or addressing a religious person or an unmarried princess or girl of noble birth)’ (OJED, s.v.).</note> Citragopta <note>The portrayal of the figure of Nini Citragopta as a female deity alongside Kaki Citragopta prior to the performance of observance in this text is particularly intriguing, as no mention of Nini Citragopta is to be found in the corpus of Old Javanese and Balinese literature. The presence of this figure brings to mind the concept of <foreign>śakti</foreign> in Śaivism. This is one of the key elements indicating the presence of a tantric spirit within this text.</note>
.
.[The request] should be received [by means of] an offering<note>I have chosen to use the word <foreign>caru</foreign> rather than the abbreviation <foreign>ca</foreign> as the abbreviation because it is not commonly found in the corpus of Old Javanese literature. Furthermore, by using the word <foreign>caru</foreign>, which means ‘to have (make, present) as an offering’ (OJED, s.v.), will help readers to understand the meaning of the term directly.</note> of a white and green betel leaf on a well. The mantra is: “My Lord Kaki Citragopta and Nini Citragopta, I ask permission to perform an observance. My Lord, please accompany me when I perform an observance! Everything that I strive after, let it be obtained! If I make a mistake when performing an observance, let it be blamed on the reverend one who is in charge of the observances!” All your observances [will then be] like that.<note>By asking permission to the Kaki Citragopta and Nini Citragopta, practitioners of the observance simultaneously seek protection from them. If they commit a mistake, that mistake is attributed to this deity. This appears to be a tactic employed by practitioners to ensure their safety while performing the observance.
.</note>
10405
.Further, the teeth-polishing leaves [have to be used] by the one who carries out the observances. The exceedingly good one is the <foreign>hambulu</foreign><note><foreign>Hambulu, ambulu</foreign> is a particular kind of tree, of the ficus family (Jb.: Ficus infectoria) (OJED, s.v.).</note>; the result is [to become] rich in gold.
.
.There are the teeth-polishing leaves of the <foreign>kayәn</foreign> <note><foreign>Kayәn</foreign> is a particular kind of tree and its flowers. In bal. com. used to render kuyaṅ, q.v. (OJED, s.v.).</note>; the result is many children.
.
10410There are the teeth-polishing leaves of the <foreign>vaṅkal</foreign> <note><foreign>Vaṅkal</foreign> is a particular kind of (wild) tree (KBW: a variety of mimosa) (OJED, s.v.).</note>; the result is [to become] rich in rice.
.
.
.There are the teeth-polishing leaves of the <foreign>lampәni</foreign><note><foreign> Lampәni</foreign> is a shrub plant that is about two meters high, the leaves are oval in shape, the young fruit tastes sour, while the old ones taste sweet and are dark red; (KBI, 2016: 717).</note>; the result is that you are successful. The dosage of all the mixtures are the same. It is appropriate to pay full attention to it.
.
10415</p>
.
.<p corresp="#tattvabrata_02">This is the <foreign>Holy Scripture</foreign>
.<note>The word <foreign>tattva</foreign> derived from Sanskrit has many meanings. The OJED defines it as ‘what something is in fact; the facts of the matter; how it really happened; the true story; the essential; the actual; the various categories of reality according to Sāmkhya doctrine; the doctrine concerning reality; the philosophy; the writings containing this doctrine; and really or in reality’ (OJED, s.v.). In this context, I have translated the word <foreign>tattva</foreign> as ‘holy scripture’, equating it with <foreign>dharma</foreign> and <foreign>jñāna</foreign> in Old Javanese. Acri (2018: 9) has provided a detailed explanation of the meaning of <foreign>tattva</foreign> and <foreign>jñāna</foreign> as ‘scripture’ in Old Javanese and Sanskrit sources to support this argument.</note> <foreign>on the Observances</foreign>.
.
10420Perfection in observances, its reality is bodiless. The Holy Dharma, its reality is [like] bars of hedge, for it serves as the tie with the reality of the observances [which keeps them together], and [it] also releases supernatural power.<note>This passage discusses the relationship between <foreign>brata</foreign>‘the observance’ and <foreign>dharma</foreign> ‘the truth’. The text explains that the reality of perfection in observances is bodiless. This is why it needs the holy truth as its body to hold everything together. Metaphorically, the truth is referred to as ‘the bars of a hedge’. Here, the metaphor ‘bars of hedge’ indicates that the truth acts as a ‘barrier’ to ensure that, after obtaining supernatural power, the practitioner of the observance still behaves in daily life under the light of Dharma and uses his supernatural power for kindness.</note>
.
.They (i.e., the observances and the Dharma) are just like the left and right bodies.<note> The left body refers to the ‘observances‘ (<foreign>brata</foreign>), and the right body refers to the ‘holy truth‘ (<foreign>dharma</foreign>). The two concepts complement each other</note>.
.
.The reality of observances and asceticism is likewise.<note>There are two interpretations regarding the use of the word ‘tapa’ here. Firstly, the word ‘tapa’ may be used in parallel with the word ‘dharma’ (‘holy truth’), as explained in the previous sentence. Secondly, the word <foreign>tapa</foreign> is actually used in conjunction with the word <foreign>brata</foreign> (‘observance’). OJED (s.v.) explains that the word <foreign>tapa</foreign> means ‘religious austerity, bodily mortification, penance, asceticism’. Often in combination with <foreign>brata</foreign>, either ‘the observance of asceticism (penance)’ or ‘penance and other religious observances’.</note>.
10425
.That is why, one who strives to obtain goodness should perform [observances and asceticism]. [If] young people perform observances, they will obtain the result of them at a young age. There is nothing that comes into being unless it is performed; there is nothing to be taken from the arrangement [according to] what has been arranged.
.
.
.As if one cooks rice in the morning and eats it that morning, one cooks rice at noon and eats it that noon, one cooks rice in the evening and eats in that evening. If one is not cooking, one is not eating. [The conclusion is that] the results are according to one’s conduct.
10430
.
.Such is the right order of [actions and results]. Because the result of bad and good conduct is obtained, that is why good conduct should be performed without delay. [This] originates from the Holy Scripture on Observances.
.</p>
.
10435
.<p corresp="#tattvabrata_03">This is “The Detailed Enumeration of the Observances”. It should be known.</p>
.
.<p corresp="#tattvabrata_1">There is the observance of ‘Cutting off the Taste’ (<foreign>Mәgat rasa</foreign>): if one eats half [portion], and stands up
.
10440<note>The literal meaning of the word <foreign>sumĕṅka</foreign> is ‘to go upwards, rise, climb’ (OJED s.v.). In this passage, I have translated it more liberal as ‘stand up’. </note>
.
.for chewing betel. It is fine if one does not speak. After chewing betel, one can eat again. Its appointed duration is one year. The deity is the Goddess Umā. The mantra is: “Om̐ Mam̐ hail to Umā!”. [I take] leave. Its result is that the love of husband and wife is not cut off, and all people love [you].</p>
.
.
10445
.
.<p corresp="#tattvabrata_2">There is the observance of eating rice from <foreign>slaṅgi</foreign><note>I have choosen the word <foreign>slaṅgi</foreign> as attested in ms. U in the Balinese, which means ‘a pyramid-shaped structure made of aren palm or jackfruit leaves used to display rice during the Kuningan festival’ (KBI, 2016: 987). I have not found the meaning of the word <foreign>ṅgi</foreign> attested in ms. G and N, as well as the word <foreign>ṅgi</foreign> as attested in ms. M, nor of <foreign>gaṅgi</foreign> as attested in ms. P.
.</note>
.
10450(<foreign>amaṅan sәga slaṅgi</foreign>): its duration is seven months. The deity is the Goddess Vastu. The mantra is: “Om̐ hail to the Goddess Vastu!” [I take ] leave. Its result is that the love of husband and wife is not cut off, and all people<note>I have emended the phrase <foreign>sama janma</foreign> attested in G M N U and <foreign>janma kabeh</foreign> attested in P to <foreign>samanta janma</foreign> ‘all people’. I made this decision in the light of previous passage 3.1 <foreign>mvaṅ samanta janma paḍa sih</foreign> ‘and all people love [you]’.</note> love you and feel sympathy for you.
.</p>
.
. <p corresp="#tattvabrata_3"> There is the observance of the ‘Earth-Leaf’ (<foreign>Bhūmipāttra</foreign>): if one eats without using leaves, and lays [the food] openly on earth. The deity is reverend Vaiśravaṇa. Its appointed duration is one year and seven months. The mantra is: “Om̐ hail to the illustrious<note> have chosen the word <foreign>śrī</foreign>, which is attested in P, instead of <foreign>Śram̐</foreign> in G, <foreign>Sam̐</foreign> in M and N, and <foreign>Śi</foreign> in U. This is because in other passages of this text, such as 3.7 <foreign>om̐ śrī ratih devyai namaḥ</foreign>, 3.10 <foreign>om̐ śrī smarāya namaḥ</foreign>, 3.11 <foreign>om̐ śrī śrī devyai namaḥ</foreign>, etc., the word <foreign>śrī</foreign> is used instead of the other <foreign>bījamantra</foreign>. The <foreign>bījamantra</foreign>s like <foreign>śram̐</foreign> in G, <foreign>sam̐</foreign> in M and N, and <foreign>śi</foreign> are not appropriate in this context. In the Indian tradition, the reverend Vaiśravaṇa is often identified with Kubera. He is the guardian of the northern direction and his home is in the northern quadrant of the topmost tier of the lower half of Mount Meru.</note> Vaiśravaṇa!” [I take ] leave. Its result is being rich in land and freeholds, and you are loved by the king and priests.
.
10455</p>
.
.
.<p corresp="#tattvabrata_4">There is the observance of ‘Craving to Embroider’ (<foreign>Anulam iḍam</foreign>)<note>I have conjectured <foreign>nulam idhan</foreign> in G, <foreign>nulam iḍam</foreign> in M, N and U, and <foreign>nulambhi nan</foreign> in P to <foreign>anulam iḍam</foreign> ‘craving to embroider’. This word has been conjectured to convey the proper meaning in Old Javanese. The word <foreign>anulam</foreign> is derived from the word <foreign>sulam</foreign>, meaning ‘to embroider’ (OJED s.v.), and the word <foreign>iḍam</foreign> means ‘to experience the cravings of pregnancy, to be pregnant’ (OJED s.v.). Thus, the word <foreign>anulam iḍam</foreign> can be translated as ‘craving to embroider’. </note>: one fast all day, until the end of the day. Its appointed duration is three months. Its result is that all desires will be obtained quickly because of that. You will be beloved by men. The deity is the Reverend Brahmā. Mantra: “Om̐ Am̐ hail to Brahmā!” [I take] leave.</p>
.
10460
.<p corresp="#tattvabrata_5">There is the observance of eating before the Reverend Sun goes down. Its appointed duration is three years. The deity of the observance is the Lord Śiva. Its result is that the mind will be clear. Your thoughts are alive <note> In this context, the phrase ‘thought will be alive’ refers to a state of mind full of inspiration. It is also suitable with the technique of the observance that has a link to the Reverend Sun as the origin of all light in this world, and is also in accordance with the belief that the Reverend Sun is the origin of all light in this world.
.</note> in one goal. Mantra: “Om̐ Mam̐ hail to Śiva!” If you apply make up.
.</p>
.
10465<p corresp="#tattvabrata_6">There is the observance of not eating when the Reverend Sun is already at sunset. Its appointed duration is one year. The deity is the Reverend Śiva. The mantra is: “om̐, hail to Śiva!” [I take] leave. Its result is that one will be knowledgeable in every kind of work, especially in learning; and one will not be ignorant in playing the <foreign>gamәlan</foreign> <note> <foreign>Gamәlan</foreign> is percussion instrument, ensemble of percussion instruments (OJED, s.v.). </note>, telling a story, and [composing] <foreign>kakavin</foreign> <note><foreign>Kakavin</foreign> is poem (in Indian metres) (OJED, s.v.).</note>; one will be handsome without equal.
.</p>
.
. <p corresp="#tattvabrata_7">There is the observance of ‘Full Moon’ (<foreign>Amūrṇama</foreign>): you are fasting every full moon. Its appointed duration is seven years and seven months. The deity is the Goddess Ratih. Mantra: “Om̐ hail to Śrī Ratih!” [I take] leave. Its result is that your work will be successful, God and Demon will love you.
.</p>
10470
.<p corresp="#tattvabrata_8">There is the observance of ‘Dark Moon’ (<foreign>Nilәm</foreign>): you are fasting every dark moon. Its appointed duration is seven months. The deity is the Goddess Rātri Devi. The mantra is: “Om̐ hail to Rātri Devi!” [I take] leave. Its result is that you will be loved by mankind; God and Demon will love you.</p>
.
.<p corresp="#tattvabrata_9">There is the observance of ‘the Abundance’ <note> In the light of Sanskrit (Monier-Williams, 1182), I translate the name of this observance, <foreign>Narasvatī</foreign>, as ‘the abundance’ instead of ‘acting like Sarasvatī’, due to the absence of a link between Sarasvatī, the goddess of knowledge, and the deity and mantra in this observance. According to the deity of this passage, Rāja Lakṣmi, who is revered as the goddess of happiness, fortune, wealth, prosperity, beauty, fertility, sovereignty and abundance, this translation is appropriate. </note> (<foreign>Narasvatī</foreign>): one does not eat the cooked rice [that is cooked with] abundant water. It is only the rice cone without meat, just salt. Its appointed duration is one year and seven months. The deity is Goddess Rāja Lakṣmi. The mantra is: “Om̐ hail to Śri Rāja Lakṣmi!” [I take] leave. Its result is that your good qualities will come out, and all your aims will be fulfilled, and then you will be famous, and you will be in harmony with your spouse.
.</p>
10475
.<p corresp="#tattvabrata_10">There is the observance of ‘Always in Bloom’ <note>Other posibility to translate this term are ‘always worshiping with flowers’, ‘always arranging flowers’, and
.‘always wearing flowers’. </note> (<foreign>Muṣpasadā</foreign>): when one should eat the flower as meat first. Its appointed duration is one year. The deity is Reverend Smara. The mantra is: “Om̐ hail to Smara!” [I take] leave. Its result is that one’s face is matchless; many [people] will love you deeply.
.</p>
.
10480<p corresp="#tattvabrata_11">There is the observance of ‘Applying Salve’ (<foreign>Ṅlepana</foreign>): when one eats the side dish<note>In Modern Javanese, the word <foreign>lalab</foreign> refers to ‘uncooked fruit and leaves eaten with rice’ (OJED, s.v.), whereas in Balinese, it refers to ‘boiled food’ (KBI, 2016: 290).</note> as meat first. Its appointed duration is three years. The deity is the Goddess Śrī. The mantra is: “Om̐ hail to Śrī!”. [I take] leave. Its result is your face being beautiful and calm, being rich in rice, many people will love you and have sympathy for you.</p>
.
.<p corresp="#tattvabrata_12">There is the observance of not chewing betel. Its appointed duration is one year, and one month. The deity is the Reverend Manodeva<note> I have choosen the word <foreign>manodeva</foreign> attested in ms. M and N, rather than <foreign>aśvino</foreign> attested in ms. G; <foreign>asvido</foreign> attested in ms. P; and <foreign>maṣnodeva</foreign> attested in ms. U because the word <foreign>manodeva</foreign> is quite similar to <foreign>Manobhava</foreign> as the god of love (see OJED s.v.). This phenomenon is probably similar to the localisation of the god Manobhu in the context of Bali. The word <foreign>manodeva</foreign> is also appropriate to the dative mantra <foreign>manodevāya</foreign> when compared to the others in this passage. Another important reason is that the result of this observance is <foreign>meṅət rūpanta manis, mvaṅ akveh bhrānta hyun iri kita</foreign>: ‘your face will be sweet and deeply loved, and many people will fall in love with you.’ This result of the observance is strongly related to the Manobhava as mentioned in 3.10 <foreign>riṅ rūpa tan pasiriṅ, akveh rәsəp asih iri kita</foreign>, and 3.203 <foreign>pinakarūpa, aśrī sumilah</foreign>.</note>. The mantra is: “Om̐ hail to Manodeva!” [I take] leave. Its result is that your face will be sweet [and] deeply loved, and many people will be sick with love for you</p>
.
.<p corresp="#tattvabrata_13">There is the observance of ‘Easy Breath’<note> Another alternative translation of <foreign>Lәga Prāṇa</foreign> is ‘Contented Life’. Literally, the word <foreign>lәga</foreign> means ‘open, satisfied, content, relieved; taking lightly, accepting, renouncing readily’ (OJED s.v.), and the word <foreign>prāṇa</foreign> means ‘1. breath; first of the five vital airs (see pañcabāyu); 2. the breath of life, life; 3. (as a seat of the feelings:) heart, soul; 4. the place on the body where one can be mortally wounded (where one’s life is located), esp. the breast; mortal (of a wound); 5. numeral coefficient for living creatures’ (OJED s.v.). </note> (<foreign>lәga prāṇa</foreign>): if one eats carrying a kris on his lap. Its appointed duration is one year and seven months. The mantra is: “Om hail to Rudra!” [I take] leave. Its result is that many people will be ready to sacrifice their lives for your life; many people will be compassionate and will love you.
10485
.</p>
.<p corresp="#tattvabrata_14">There is the observance of ‘Hero’<note>I assume that the word <foreign>bīra</foreign> here is the other form of <foreign>vīra</foreign> which is refers to brave man, hero, valiant warrior; brave, valiant (OJED s.v.). This phenomenon is often in Old Javanese, for instance the word <foreign>bulan</foreign> ‘moon’ also has other form as <foreign>vulan</foreign>.</note> (<foreign>Bīra</foreign>): if one eats salt as meat. Its appointed duration is one year and three months. The deity is the Lord Iśvara. The mantra is: “Om̐ Mam̐ hail to Īśvara!” [I take] leave. Its result is that all your efforts will be achieved quickly; you will be loved by mankind, and the Gods [and] the Demons will love you.
.</p>
.
10490
.<p corresp="#tattvabrata_15">There is the observance of not eating the betel leaf [rubbed] by lime. Its appointed duration is one year. The deity is the Goddess Bhagāvati. The mantra is: “Om̐ hail to Bhagāvati!” [I take] leave. Its result is being free from all poisons; there will be no obstacle upon you.</p>
.
.<p corresp="#tattvabrata_16">There is the observance of eating the leaves on which food is served. Its appointed duration is seven years. The deity is the Lord Īśvara. The mantra is: “Om̐ hail to Īśvara” <note>An interesting textual phenomenon can be observed here. The mss. M, N and U contain the mantra: <foreign>om̐ mam̐ īśvarāya namaḥ</foreign>, whereas G contains the mantra: <foreign><foreign>mantra kadi ṅuni</foreign></foreign>, meaning ‘the mantra is as before’. This phenomenon goes beyond lexical synonymy, but is a synonym in syntax scope. The ms. G refers to a previous mantra that already exists in the initial passage (4v-5r), which contains <foreign>om̐ mam̐ iśvarāya namaḥ</foreign>.</note>. [I take] leave. Its result is to reach the heaven of Lord Īśvara. [Alternatively, if] something goes wrong, you will be reborn as a clothes vendor<note>I have chosen the word <foreign>basana</foreign> in ms. G instead of the word <foreign>bhāṣa</foreign> because of the parallel with the MM in passage 5 (<foreign>hana brata akarvan patrāhāra ṅaranya, pituṅ tahun samayanya, ⟨phalanya⟩ mulih mariṅ svarga saṅ hyaṅ iśvara, sasarnya ajanma riṅ juru basana, sugih hulun, labdha ri saṅ prabhu.</foreign>). The word <foreign>basana</foreign> in was derived from the Sanskrit word <foreign>vasana</foreign> ‘clothes, garment, attire’ (see OJED, s.v.).
.</note>, rich in servants, successful with the king and his minister, [and] you will not be unsurpassed by all your companions<note>Lexically, the sentence tan pada lavan rovaṅta kabeh can be translated as ‘you will not be equal to all your companions’. I translated this sentence more liberal as ‘unsurpassed by all your companions’. </note>.
10495</p>
.
.
.
.<p corresp="#tattvabrata_17">There is the observance of ‘Eating Fruit (especially edible roots and fruits)’ (<foreign>Ṅraka</foreign>) <note>I have choosen the word <foreign>ṅraka</foreign> as attested in mss. M N and U as a kind of a vernacular form of Old Javanese in Bali which is not attested in OJED. However, the meaning is the same with the word <foreign>araka</foreign> which means ‘taking, seizing, robbing, food (esp. edible roots and fruit?)’ as attested in ms. G.
10500</note>: one eats every kind of fruit. Its appointed duration is three years. Its deity is the Reverend Īśvara. The mantra is: “Om̐ mam̐ hail to Śiva!” <note>Mss. M P and U contains the mantra: <foreign>om̐ mam̐ ⟨śivā⟩ya namaḥ svāhā</foreign>, whereas the ms. G <foreign>contains mantra kadi ṅūni</foreign>. See my footnote in passage 3.16.
.</note>[I take] leave. Its result is reaching the abode of the Lord Śiva. [Alternatively, if] something goes wrong, you will be reborn as a wise priest, rich in silver, successful with the king and ministers. </p>
.
.
.
10505<p corresp="#tattvabrata_18">There is the observance of ‘Behaving like Kumbhakarṇa’ (<foreign>Aṅumbhakarṇa</foreign>)<note>This observance is interesting because it imitates the behavior of Kumbhakarṇa as a young brother of Rāvāṇa in the Rāmāyaṇa epic. On the basis of Kakavin Rāmāyaṇa, the figure of Kumbhakarṇa is always sleeping. However he woke up when he heard the quintessence speech of his grandfather. The Kakavin Rāmāyaṇa mentions the figure of Kumbhakarṇa as follows: Kāla saṅ kaki sәḍәṅ mavara-varah, Kumbhakarṇa sira jagra ya rumәṅə̄, de nikari ujar-ujar pasili-silih, śīghra yar pavuṅu arddha warurutәn. When his grandfather was giving his admonishment, Kumbhakarṇa woke up, and on hearing the conversation quickly became attentive, though still very sleepy (see Santoso, 1980: 358).</note>: when one sleeps on one side [position] for one year, lies on the back face up for one year, [then] lies face downwards for one year. Its appointed duration is three years. The deity of the observance is the Lord Rudra. The mantra is: Om̐ hail to Rudra! [I take] leave. Its result is that you will be loved by the learned men; all humans will respect you; all your aims will be successful.</p>
.
.
.
.<p corresp="#tattvabrata_19">Furthermore, if one is silent when defecating, the desire <note>I have translated the word <foreign>prih</foreign> as ‘desire’, as this is its meaning in Balinese (KBI, 2016: 730). OJED (s.v.) defines the word prih as ‘effort, exertion, full attention, great care and devotion’.
10510</note> is achieved quickly, [and] you will have many disciples.</p>
.
.
.
.<p corresp="#tattvabrata_20">And, if you are silent when sweeping, the result is that you will be loved by the learned man as well as gods and rulers; [your] reincarnation will be good.</p>
10515
.
.
.<p corresp="#tattvabrata_21">And, if you are silent when polishing teeth, the result is that your purpose will be achieved. </p>
.
10520
.
.<p corresp="#tattvabrata_22">And, if one is silent when applying the [holy] ash (bhasma), the result is that one reaches the abode of the Goddess Rātri. [Alternatively, if] something goes wrong, one is reborn as a learned man.
.</p>
.
10525
.
.<p corresp="#tattvabrata_23"></p>
.<p corresp="#tattvabrata_24"></p>
.<p corresp="#tattvabrata_25"></p>
10530<p corresp="#tattvabrata_26"></p>
.<p corresp="#tattvabrata_27"></p>
.<p corresp="#tattvabrata_28"></p>
.
.
10535<p corresp="#tattvabrata_29">There is an observance when one eats following the moonlight (<foreign>Anūtakәn Vulan</foreign>). The technical details are as follows. On the first day after the waxing moon, [you eat only] a handful. If the waxing period of the moon increases, it [should be] added by a handful until fifteen handfuls when the full moon, because it adds a handful every day. However, on the waning moon, it should decrease by a handful every day. Finally, one fasts when the dark moon. Its appointed duration is three months.
.The deity is the Lord Indra. Mantra: “Om̐ salutations to god Indra!” [I take leave].
.
.Its result is to reach the heaven of the Lord Śiva. [Alternatively, if] something goes wrong, one is reborn as a smart king, and the priest who has many disciples. 
.</p>

10870<p corresp="#tattvabrata_279">There is the observance of ‘thursday’: the manner is one fasts every thursday. Its result is that you will be beautiful, and all your works will be good.</p>
.<p corresp="#tattvabrata_280"></p>

10915<p corresp="#tattvabrata_318">There is the observance of ‘Being Glow’ (<foreign>Mārab</foreign>)
. <note>I have conjectured the word <foreign>mūrāba</foreign> as <foreign>mārab</foreign>, as the former does not appear in the OJED or Balinese dictionaries. I assume that <foreign>mūraba</foreign> is a mystical form of <foreign>mārab</foreign>, which means ‘to flare, flame, blaze, glow’ (OJED, s.v.). It is also consistent with the technique of performing the observance, whereby the practitioner eats certain types of flowers.</note>
.
.: one should start performing the observance on the fourth day of the waxing moon. One should eat the flower of <foreign>nāgasāri</foreign> (<foreign>Mesua ferrea</foreign>), <foreign>pūraṇa</foreign> (Clitoria ternatea) <note>Nāgasāri: According to the text titled <foreign>Kavi Jānaki</foreign>, collected in Unit Lontar, Udayana University. I found the word <foreign>purāṇa</foreign> used to designate one plant, namely <foreign>itil</foreign>. The text contains: <foreign>krĕntikā, smaracatrā, wagaprańā, puranā, gamantya ṅa itil</foreign> (<foreign>Kavi Jānaki</foreign>, 16r). In the oral tradition, the word itil refers to the <foreign>talaṅ </foreign>flower (Clitoria ternatea).</note>,
.
10920 [and] <foreign>kulalaṭa</foreign> <note>I have not found the specific plant to which <foreign>kulalaṭa</foreign> refers. OJED (s.v.) explains that <foreign>lalaṭa</foreign> is a particular kind of flower or floral motif. </note>.
.
. It should end on the full moon. Its result is being handsome [or] beautiful without equal. The mantra is: ’Oṃ hail to Smara! [It is recited] when applying make-up. </p>
.
.
10925
.<p corresp="#tattvabrata_319">There is the observance<note>This passage does not provide a detailed explanation of the technique for performing the observance. I assume that the word <foreign>mopavāsa</foreign> ‘fasting’ is needed here to complete the explanation. The word <foreign>brata</foreign> itself also has the meaning of a ‘holy practice’ (fasting, continence, etc.) (OJED, s.v.).</note> [perfomed] on the eleventh day of the waxing moon. It is called ‘beyond the smoke’ (<foreign>Atikukus</foreign>). Its result is becoming a brave man, [and] being perfectly prosperous.
.</p>
.
.
10930
.<p corresp="#tattvabrata_320">There is the observance of eating half cooked-rice
.
. <note>I translate <foreign>aron-aron</foreign> as ‘half-cooked rice’ rather than ‘with leaves’ (variant form of <foreign>aron-ron</foreign>). I assume the word <foreign>aron-aron</foreign> was derived from the words <foreign>haru</foreign> or <foreign>aru</foreign>. In Old Javanese, <foreign>haru</foreign>-<foreign>daṅ</foreign> means ‘a pot for half-cooked rice’ and <foreign>paṅarvan</foreign> means ‘a pot in which half-cooked rice is stirred before being put back in the <foreign>kukusan</foreign>’ (ModJ) (OJED, s.v.). In Balinese, the words <foreign>haru</foreign>/<foreign>aru</foreign> + -an become <foreign>aruwan</foreign>/<foreign>aron</foreign> (another instance for this sound change is: <foreign>kalaṅvan</foreign> → <foreign>kalaṅon</foreign>/<foreign>kalaṅәn</foreign>, <foreign>vvaṅ</foreign> → <foreign>voṅ</foreign>, etc. ), meaning ‘half-cooked rice’.
.</note>,
10935
. [and] burning coconuts. Its appointed duration is fifteen days. The deity of the observance is the Reverend Viśeṣa. Its result is a beautiful head.
.</p>
.
.
10940
. <p corresp="#tattvabrata_321">There is the observance of eating without using a leaf [as a plate]. Its appointed duration is seven months. Its result is that one’s actions are successful. The name of such observance is ‘Record of Victory’ (<foreign>Jayapattra</foreign>) <note>OJED (s.v.) defines the term <foreign>jayapattra</foreign> as ‘a record of victory (in a lawsuit) given to the victorious party’. In this context, I only use ‘record of victory’ to make the translation <foreign>jayapattra</foreign> more precise.
.</note>.
.</p>
.
10945
.
.<p corresp="#tattvabrata_322">There is an observance that over powers all [other] observances. Its result is reaching the heaven of the Lord Umapati. [Alternatively, if] something goes wrong one will reborn as a world ruler; being a powerful priest who has many disciples; having received fame as a gift.</p>
.
.
10950
.<p corresp="#tattvabrata_323">There is the observance of being like a child who will not keep a secret. Its result is that you are not reincarnated repeatedly. [Alternatively, if] something goes wrong, one is reborn as a king.</p>
.
.
.
10955<p corresp="#tattvabrata_324">There is the observance of putting out the fire, chewing betel for three days, [and] not eating all kinds [of food]. It is finished after three days<note>Other alternatives for this translation is ‘the food is taken after abstinence for three days’.</note>, and should be sprinkled with holy water. Its result is that all of one’s pain vanishes. </p>
.
.
.
. <p corresp="#tattvabrata_325">There is the observance of consuming <foreign>sәsәḍĕp</foreign><note><foreign>Sәsәḍep</foreign> is finely chopped betel etc with <foreign>dadap</foreign> leaves, <foreign>bras</foreign> and <foreign>kuñit</foreign> used as <foreign>bhasma</foreign> on the temples, between the eyes, on the head and the shoulder-blades (esp. in certain ceremonies) (OJED s.v.)</note> before the other. Its appointed duration is seven years. The deity of the observance is the Goddess Vastu. Its result is being obeyed by mankind.
10960</p>
.
.
.
.<p corresp="#tattvabrata_326">There is the observance of eating the salt mix with charcoal as meat. Its result is being obeyed by mankind, being followed by the world, [and] being feared by enemies.
10965</p>
.
.
.
.<p corresp="#tattvabrata_327">There is the observance of eating the [cooked rice] with four colours. Its appointed duration is five nights. Its result is becoming smart [and] powerful, and then being loved by mankind. You [will become] prominent. The name of such observance is <foreign>sakabdhu</foreign> <note> The word <foreign>sakabdhu</foreign> does not exist in OJED and Balinese dictionaries. I have not found any interpretations of this word yet.</note></p>
10970
.
.
.<p corresp="#tattvabrata_328">There is the observance of eating during the day, five [times]
.<note>The number 5 in the text is not clearly explained. For the time being, this number 5 is interpreted as ‘5 times’. I put it in the brackets. Another possibility is ‘5 handfuls of food per day’.
10975</note>. Its result is that your fingers and skin will be fine.</p>
.
.
.
.<p corresp="#tattvabrata_329">There is the observance of ‘Following Interval’ (<foreign>Ṅantāra</foreign>): one eats in the middle of the day, [and] in the middle of the night. Its appointed duration for repeated exercise is three months. Its result is that all your descendants become powerful, [and experience] great happiness. </p>
10980
.
.
.<p corresp="#tattvabrata_330">There is the observance of eating seven handfuls [of food] in one day. Its appointed duration to perform the observance is seven days. The name of the observance is four (<foreign>Catur</foreign>) <note>I have not found yet the releation between the name of this observance <foreign>catur</foreign> ‘four’ with the technique to perform the observance and the duration.</note>. Its result<note> For the reason in adding the word <foreign>pha,</foreign> in this passage see footnote 3.331.</note> is that you will be reborn as a person with a body unaffected by any type of iron in the invisible realm. </p>
.
10985
.
.<p corresp="#tattvabrata_331">There is the observance of eating without sitting. The Reverend Hayu gives the observance. The name of the observance is the Reverend of Walking (<foreign>Saṅ Hyaṅ Laku</foreign>). He serves as an appearance who is beautifully attractive. Its result
.
. <note>I have added the word pha, meaning ‘its result’ in accordance with the general pattern found in other passages of the Tattva Brata. <foreign>Pha</foreign> is typically placed after the mantra portion: <foreign>ma, om̐ śambhave namaḥ, pamit, pha, mañjanma riṅ kulaputra</foreign> (3.26); after the duration of the brata: <foreign>tigaṅ tahun lavasnya, pha, drәman aputra, siṅ prih meṅgal katəkan</foreign> (3.27); after the technical details of the <foreign>brata</foreign>’s performance: <foreign>hana brata tan pamaṅan ivak bavi, pha, tan kataman deniṅ sarvaviṣya</foreign> (3.63), after the name of the brata: <foreign>saṅ hyaṅ kr̥ta bhuvana hyaṅniṅ brata, pha</foreign>, etc. (3.87).</note>
10990
. is being happy in your journey; the ash of your trace is followed by attendants; you will be successful with happiness and wealth; you will enjoy the palace in the future.
.</p>
.
.
10995
.<p corresp="#tattvabrata_332">There is the observance of ‘Behaving like Open Hall’ (<foreign>Maṇḍapa</foreign>): one eats in the lap using the leaves as a base. The Reverend Sūkṣma gives the observance. Its result is that all your deeds are fit (completely right), [and] your relationship with your spouse is not cut off. Its appointed duration is one month. The mantra is: “Om̐ hail to the [Reverend] Sūkṣma!” [I take] leave.</p>
.
.
.
11000<p corresp="#tattvabrata_333">There is the observance of not eating all kinds of breathing beings every <foreign>Pon</foreign> <note><foreign>Pon</foreign> is the third day in the five-day cycle (<foreign>pañcavāra</foreign>) of the Old Javanese/Balinese calendar system. </note> and <foreign>Kalivon</foreign> <note><foreign>Kalivon</foreign> is the fifth day in the five-day cycle (<foreign>pañcavāra)</foreign> of the Old Javanese/Balinese calendar system.</note>day. Its result is being obeyed by mankind.
.</p>
.
.
.
11005<p corresp="#tattvabrata_334">There is the observance of eating while looking in the mirror every full moon day. Its appointed duration is one year. Its result is being reborn as a rich senior customary village head (<foreign>kabayan buyut</foreign>)
.
.<note> The word <foreign>kabayan</foreign> means ‘old; an elder, chief, leader’ (OJED, s.v.), while <foreign>buyut</foreign> means ‘great-grandfather, great-grandchild; elder’ (OJED, s.v.). In the Balinese context, the word <foreign>kabayan</foreign> refers to a ‘customary village head’ (KBI, 2016: 96). For this reason, in this context, I translate <foreign>kabayan buyut</foreign> as ‘senior customary village head’.
.</note>.
.</p>
11010
.
.
.<p corresp="#tattvabrata_335">This is the sacred text on the hair (<foreign>Aji Rambut</foreign>): one eats the black cooked rice every fourth day of the bright half of the lunar month. The mantra is: “I am performing the sacred teaching of the hair that is not red, not transparent, not white. May my hair be black just like a crow: long, soft
. <note>I have emended the word <foreign>alambas</foreign> to <foreign>alәmәs</foreign>. The Balinese word <foreign>alambas</foreign> meaning ‘long’ (KBI, 2016: 540) is already expressed by the word <foreign>adavā</foreign> ‘long’ (OJED, s.v.) in the previous word in this sentence. The word <foreign>alәmәs</foreign> meaning ‘pliant, lithe, lissom, supple, slender, and soft’ (OJED, s.v.) is a more suitable choice in this context as the main topic is about the hair. </note>,
11015 [and] thick. It is obtained presently. I am performing the sacred teaching of hair, which is good presently. Surely, I am performing the sacred teaching of hair. Om̐ Sa Ba Ta A I! Hail to Śiva!” </p>
.
.
.
.<p corresp="#tattvabrata_336">There is the observance of being silent in worship. Its result is that you will be loved by God. </p>
11020
.
.
.<p corresp="#tattvabrata_337">There is the observance of being silent when defecating, urinating, taking a bath, applying oil, wearing undergarments, [and] walking. Its appointed duration is seven months. Lord Śiva gives the observance. [Alternatively, if] something goes wrong, one will be rich in property, rich in offspring, and be obeyed [by people], [as well as] being reborn as a minister. </p>
.
11025
.
.<p corresp="#tattvabrata_338">In 1722 <foreign>Śaka</foreign> (1800 AD), on Thursday <foreign>Kalivon</foreign>, <foreign>Vāra Marakih</foreign><note><foreign>Marakih</foreign> is the name of the 16th vuku (OJED, s.v.)</note>, on the first day of the bright lunar fortnight in the month <foreign>Asuji</foreign> (September-October). The unit is two. The tens are two. That is the time when it is completely written.<note>This manuscript was completed at the end of the 18th century.</note></p>
.</div>
.<!-- translation content-->
11030
.
.
.

hana brata yan amaṅan anūtakǝn vulan ... śiṣya təka; in P the title of the brata, mantra, and result is same with other witnesses, but tend to different in the technique to perform the observance. This is the complete passage of the ms P. "hana brata hañutakәn hulan·, yan amaṅan taṅgal hapisan·, sakәpәl·, taṅ, 2, rvaṅ kәpәl·, muṅgah sakәpәl· sadinā, tәkāniṅ taṅgal·, piṅ, 14, pūrnama hamr̥ti, yan paṅloṅ hapisan·, piṅ, 14, sinuddhana sakәpәl·, tәkaniṅ til̥m hamr̥ti, tigaṅ lek· ṣamayanya, bhaṭārendra hyaṅnya, ma, Ōm̐ surendra ya namaḥ, pamit·. phalanya mantukiṅ bhaṭāra śivā, sasarnya mañjanmā riṅ ratu, mvaṅ riṅ vikva bhavu siṣyā kitā." mrakih NThis […] Behaviour According to the context of this passage, which explains the right behaviour when performing an observance, such as asking permission from the one who in charge in observance, offering betel leaves and reciting mantras, I have chosen parikramaning ‘proper order of things, right behaviour, customs (ritual) sanctioned by tradition’ (OJED, s.v.), as attested in mss. N and M. This is instead of panarima, probably a non-standard form of panariman ‘he who is given st., recipient’ (OJED, s.v.) as attested in mss. G and P, or tiṅkahiṅ panarima, meaning ‘way of acting for the recipient’ (the meaning of the word tiṅkah in OJED s.v.) as attested in ms. U. The words parikrama, panarima and tiṅkahiṅ panarima in Old Javanese have similar meanings. In the context of observance, the word parikramaniṅ brata emphasises the process of systematic conduct when performing the observance. Conversely, the word panarima brata and tiṅkahiṅ panarima brata emphasises the preparation of the practitioner before performing the observance. in [Performing] Observances. When you perform an observance, do not do it haphazardly, without having permission to the one who is in charge of the observances, [namely] the reverend KakiThe word kaki means ‘grandfather; old man, elder; venerable’ (OJED, s.v.). CitragoptaCitragopta or Citragupta is the keeper of the records of the good and evil deeds of human beings for Yama, and as such is well-known both from Skt. and OJ. literature (his name is also given as Citragotra. In Balinese tradition, he has a famous name as Saṅ Surātma). In Kakavin Śivarātrikalpa as already mentioned by Teeuw et al. (1969: 52) he reads a book with full account of one’s deed during one’s life. In India the book is called Agrasandhāni; in the Kakavin Śivarātrikalpa it is called a galih, but no specific name is given. [and] NiniThe word nini means ‘grandmother; woman (used in designating or addressing a religious person or an unmarried princess or girl of noble birth)’ (OJED, s.v.). Citragopta The portrayal of the figure of Nini Citragopta as a female deity alongside Kaki Citragopta prior to the performance of observance in this text is particularly intriguing, as no mention of Nini Citragopta is to be found in the corpus of Old Javanese and Balinese literature. The presence of this figure brings to mind the concept of śakti in Śaivism. This is one of the key elements indicating the presence of a tantric spirit within this text. [The request] should be received [by means of] an offeringI have chosen to use the word caru rather than the abbreviation ca as the abbreviation because it is not commonly found in the corpus of Old Javanese literature. Furthermore, by using the word caru, which means ‘to have (make, present) as an offering’ (OJED, s.v.), will help readers to understand the meaning of the term directly. of a white and green betel leaf on a well. The mantra is: “My Lord Kaki Citragopta and Nini Citragopta, I ask permission to perform an observance. My Lord, please accompany me when I perform an observance! Everything that I strive after, let it be obtained! If I make a mistake when performing an observance, let it be blamed on the reverend one who is in charge of the observances!” All your observances [will then be] like that.By asking permission to the Kaki Citragopta and Nini Citragopta, practitioners of the observance simultaneously seek protection from them. If they commit a mistake, that mistake is attributed to this deity. This appears to be a tactic employed by practitioners to ensure their safety while performing the observance. Further, the teeth-polishing leaves [have to be used] by the one who carries out the observances. The exceedingly good one is the hambuluHambulu, ambulu is a particular kind of tree, of the ficus family (Jb.: Ficus infectoria) (OJED, s.v.).; the result is [to become] rich in gold. There are the teeth-polishing leaves of the kayәn Kayәn is a particular kind of tree and its flowers. In bal. com. used to render kuyaṅ, q.v. (OJED, s.v.).; the result is many children. There are the teeth-polishing leaves of the vaṅkal Vaṅkal is a particular kind of (wild) tree (KBW: a variety of mimosa) (OJED, s.v.).; the result is [to become] rich in rice. There are the teeth-polishing leaves of the lampәni Lampәni is a shrub plant that is about two meters high, the leaves are oval in shape, the young fruit tastes sour, while the old ones taste sweet and are dark red; (KBI, 2016: 717).; the result is that you are successful. The dosage of all the mixtures are the same. It is appropriate to pay full attention to it.

[The request] should be received [by means of] an offeringI have chosen to use the word caru rather than the abbreviation ca as the abbreviation because it is not commonly found in the corpus of Old Javanese literature. Furthermore, by using the word caru, which means ‘to have (make, present) as an offering’ (OJED, s.v.), will help readers to understand the meaning of the term directly. of a white and green betel leaf on a well. The mantra is: “My Lord Kaki Citragopta and Nini Citragopta, I ask permission to perform an observance. My Lord, please accompany me when I perform an observance! Everything that I strive after, let it be obtained! If I make a mistake when performing an observance, let it be blamed on the reverend one who is in charge of the observances!” All your observances [will then be] like that.By asking permission to the Kaki Citragopta and Nini Citragopta, practitioners of the observance simultaneously seek protection from them. If they commit a mistake, that mistake is attributed to this deity. This appears to be a tactic employed by practitioners to ensure their safety while performing the observance. Further, the teeth-polishing leaves [have to be used] by the one who carries out the observances. The exceedingly good one is the hambuluHambulu, ambulu is a particular kind of tree, of the ficus family (Jb.: Ficus infectoria) (OJED, s.v.).; the result is [to become] rich in gold. There are the teeth-polishing leaves of the kayәn Kayәn is a particular kind of tree and its flowers. In bal. com. used to render kuyaṅ, q.v. (OJED, s.v.).; the result is many children. There are the teeth-polishing leaves of the vaṅkal Vaṅkal is a particular kind of (wild) tree (KBW: a variety of mimosa) (OJED, s.v.).; the result is [to become] rich in rice. There are the teeth-polishing leaves of the lampәni Lampәni is a shrub plant that is about two meters high, the leaves are oval in shape, the young fruit tastes sour, while the old ones taste sweet and are dark red; (KBI, 2016: 717).; the result is that you are successful. The dosage of all the mixtures are the same. It is appropriate to pay full attention to it.
I have chosen to use the word caru rather than the abbreviation ca as the abbreviation because it is not commonly found in the corpus of Old Javanese literature. Furthermore, by using the word caru, which means ‘to have (make, present) as an offering’ (OJED, s.v.), will help readers to understand the meaning of the term directly.This […] Behaviour According to the context of this passage, which explains the right behaviour when performing an observance, such as asking permission from the one who in charge in observance, offering betel leaves and reciting mantras, I have chosen parikramaning ‘proper order of things, right behaviour, customs (ritual) sanctioned by tradition’ (OJED, s.v.), as attested in mss. N and M. This is instead of panarima, probably a non-standard form of panariman ‘he who is given st., recipient’ (OJED, s.v.) as attested in mss. G and P, or tiṅkahiṅ panarima, meaning ‘way of acting for the recipient’ (the meaning of the word tiṅkah in OJED s.v.) as attested in ms. U. The words parikrama, panarima and tiṅkahiṅ panarima in Old Javanese have similar meanings. In the context of observance, the word parikramaniṅ brata emphasises the process of systematic conduct when performing the observance. Conversely, the word panarima brata and tiṅkahiṅ panarima brata emphasises the preparation of the practitioner before performing the observance. in [Performing] Observances. When you perform an observance, do not do it haphazardly, without having permission to the one who is in charge of the observances, [namely] the reverend KakiThe word kaki means ‘grandfather; old man, elder; venerable’ (OJED, s.v.). CitragoptaCitragopta or Citragupta is the keeper of the records of the good and evil deeds of human beings for Yama, and as such is well-known both from Skt. and OJ. literature (his name is also given as Citragotra. In Balinese tradition, he has a famous name as Saṅ Surātma). In Kakavin Śivarātrikalpa as already mentioned by Teeuw et al. (1969: 52) he reads a book with full account of one’s deed during one’s life. In India the book is called Agrasandhāni; in the Kakavin Śivarātrikalpa it is called a galih, but no specific name is given. [and] NiniThe word nini means ‘grandmother; woman (used in designating or addressing a religious person or an unmarried princess or girl of noble birth)’ (OJED, s.v.). Lampәni is a shrub plant that is about two meters high, the leaves are oval in shape, the young fruit tastes sour, while the old ones taste sweet and are dark red; (KBI, 2016: 717).This […] Scripture The word tattva derived from Sanskrit has many meanings. The OJED defines it as ‘what something is in fact; the facts of the matter; how it really happened; the true story; the essential; the actual; the various categories of reality according to Sāmkhya doctrine; the doctrine concerning reality; the philosophy; the writings containing this doctrine; and really or in reality’ (OJED, s.v.). In this context, I have translated the word tattva as ‘holy scripture’, equating it with dharma and jñāna in Old Javanese. Acri (2018: 9) has provided a detailed explanation of the meaning of tattva and jñāna as ‘scripture’ in Old Javanese and Sanskrit sources to support this argument. on the Observances. Perfection in observances, its reality is bodiless. The Holy Dharma, its reality is [like] bars of hedge, for it serves as the tie with the reality of the observances [which keeps them together], and [it] also releases supernatural power.This passage discusses the relationship between brata‘the observance’ and dharma ‘the truth’. The text explains that the reality of perfection in observances is bodiless. This is why it needs the holy truth as its body to hold everything together. Metaphorically, the truth is referred to as ‘the bars of a hedge’. Here, the metaphor ‘bars of hedge’ indicates that the truth acts as a ‘barrier’ to ensure that, after obtaining supernatural power, the practitioner of the observance still behaves in daily life under the light of Dharma and uses his supernatural power for kindness. They (i.e., the observances and the Dharma) are just like the left and right bodies. The left body refers to the ‘observances‘ (brata), and the right body refers to the ‘holy truth‘ (dharma). The two concepts complement each other. The reality of observances and asceticism is likewise.There are two interpretations regarding the use of the word ‘tapa’ here. Firstly, the word ‘tapa’ may be used in parallel with the word ‘dharma’ (‘holy truth’), as explained in the previous sentence. Secondly, the word tapa is actually used in conjunction with the word brata (‘observance’). OJED (s.v.) explains that the word tapa means ‘religious austerity, bodily mortification, penance, asceticism’. Often in combination with brata, either ‘the observance of asceticism (penance)’ or ‘penance and other religious observances’.. That is why, one who strives to obtain goodness should perform [observances and asceticism]. [If] young people perform observances, they will obtain the result of them at a young age. There is nothing that comes into being unless it is performed; there is nothing to be taken from the arrangement [according to] what has been arranged. As if one cooks rice in the morning and eats it that morning, one cooks rice at noon and eats it that noon, one cooks rice in the evening and eats in that evening. If one is not cooking, one is not eating. [The conclusion is that] the results are according to one’s conduct. Such is the right order of [actions and results]. Because the result of bad and good conduct is obtained, that is why good conduct should be performed without delay. [This] originates from the Holy Scripture on Observances.
The word tattva derived from Sanskrit has many meanings. The OJED defines it as ‘what something is in fact; the facts of the matter; how it really happened; the true story; the essential; the actual; the various categories of reality according to Sāmkhya doctrine; the doctrine concerning reality; the philosophy; the writings containing this doctrine; and really or in reality’ (OJED, s.v.). In this context, I have translated the word tattva as ‘holy scripture’, equating it with dharma and jñāna in Old Javanese. Acri (2018: 9) has provided a detailed explanation of the meaning of tattva and jñāna as ‘scripture’ in Old Javanese and Sanskrit sources to support this argument.This […] Scripture The word tattva derived from Sanskrit has many meanings. The OJED defines it as ‘what something is in fact; the facts of the matter; how it really happened; the true story; the essential; the actual; the various categories of reality according to Sāmkhya doctrine; the doctrine concerning reality; the philosophy; the writings containing this doctrine; and really or in reality’ (OJED, s.v.). In this context, I have translated the word tattva as ‘holy scripture’, equating it with dharma and jñāna in Old Javanese. Acri (2018: 9) has provided a detailed explanation of the meaning of tattva and jñāna as ‘scripture’ in Old Javanese and Sanskrit sources to support this argument. on the Observances. Perfection in observances, its reality is bodiless. The Holy Dharma, its reality is [like] bars of hedge, for it serves as the tie with the reality of the observances [which keeps them together], and [it] also releases supernatural power.This passage discusses the relationship between brata‘the observance’ and dharma ‘the truth’. The text explains that the reality of perfection in observances is bodiless. This is why it needs the holy truth as its body to hold everything together. Metaphorically, the truth is referred to as ‘the bars of a hedge’. Here, the metaphor ‘bars of hedge’ indicates that the truth acts as a ‘barrier’ to ensure that, after obtaining supernatural power, the practitioner of the observance still behaves in daily life under the light of Dharma and uses his supernatural power for kindness. They (i.e., the observances and the Dharma) are just like the left and right bodies. The left body refers to the ‘observances‘ (brata), and the right body refers to the ‘holy truth‘ (dharma). The two concepts complement each other. The reality of observances and asceticism is likewise.There are two interpretations regarding the use of the word ‘tapa’ here. Firstly, the word ‘tapa’ may be used in parallel with the word ‘dharma’ (‘holy truth’), as explained in the previous sentence. Secondly, the word tapa is actually used in conjunction with the word brata (‘observance’). OJED (s.v.) explains that the word tapa means ‘religious austerity, bodily mortification, penance, asceticism’. Often in combination with brata, either ‘the observance of asceticism (penance)’ or ‘penance and other religious observances’.. That is why, one who strives to obtain goodness should perform [observances and asceticism]. [If] young people perform observances, they will obtain the result of them at a young age. There is nothing that comes into being unless it is performed; there is nothing to be taken from the arrangement [according to] what has been arranged. As if one cooks rice in the morning and eats it that morning, one cooks rice at noon and eats it that noon, one cooks rice in the evening and eats in that evening. If one is not cooking, one is not eating. [The conclusion is that] the results are according to one’s conduct. Such is the right order of [actions and results]. Because the result of bad and good conduct is obtained, that is why good conduct should be performed without delay. [This] originates from the Holy Scripture on Observances.

have chosen the word śrī, which is attested in P, instead of Śram̐ in G, Sam̐ in M and N, and Śi in U. This is because in other passages of this text, such as 3.7 om̐ śrī ratih devyai namaḥ, 3.10 om̐ śrī smarāya namaḥ, 3.11 om̐ śrī śrī devyai namaḥ, etc., the word śrī is used instead of the other bījamantra. The bījamantras like śram̐ in G, sam̐ in M and N, and śi are not appropriate in this context. In the Indian tradition, the reverend Vaiśravaṇa is often identified with Kubera. He is the guardian of the northern direction and his home is in the northern quadrant of the topmost tier of the lower half of Mount Meru.There […] leave.
I have conjectured nulam idhan in G, nulam iḍam in M, N and U, and nulambhi nan in P to anulam iḍam ‘craving to embroider’. This word has been conjectured to convey the proper meaning in Old Javanese. The word anulam is derived from the word sulam, meaning ‘to embroider’ (OJED s.v.), and the word iḍam means ‘to experience the cravings of pregnancy, to be pregnant’ (OJED s.v.). Thus, the word anulam iḍam can be translated as ‘craving to embroider’. There […] world. in one goal. Mantra: “Om̐ Mam̐ hail to Śiva!” If you apply make up.

In the light of Sanskrit (Monier-Williams, 1182), I translate the name of this observance, Narasvatī, as ‘the abundance’ instead of ‘acting like Sarasvatī’, due to the absence of a link between Sarasvatī, the goddess of knowledge, and the deity and mantra in this observance. According to the deity of this passage, Rāja Lakṣmi, who is revered as the goddess of happiness, fortune, wealth, prosperity, beauty, fertility, sovereignty and abundance, this translation is appropriate. The mantra is: “Om̐ hail to Smara!” [I take] leave. Its result is that one’s face is matchless; many [people] will love you deeply.
Other posibility to translate this term are ‘always worshiping with flowers’, ‘always arranging flowers’, and ‘always wearing flowers’. There […] you.

I have choosen the word manodeva attested in ms. M and N, rather than aśvino attested in ms. G; asvido attested in ms. P; and maṣnodeva attested in ms. U because the word manodeva is quite similar to Manobhava as the god of love (see OJED s.v.). This phenomenon is probably similar to the localisation of the god Manobhu in the context of Bali. The word manodeva is also appropriate to the dative mantra manodevāya when compared to the others in this passage. Another important reason is that the result of this observance is meṅət rūpanta manis, mvaṅ akveh bhrānta hyun iri kita: ‘your face will be sweet and deeply loved, and many people will fall in love with you.’ This result of the observance is strongly related to the Manobhava as mentioned in 3.10 riṅ rūpa tan pasiriṅ, akveh rәsəp asih iri kita, and 3.203 pinakarūpa, aśrī sumilah.There […] you.

(as a seat of the feelings:) heart, soul; 4. the place on the body where one can be mortally wounded (where one’s life is located), esp. the breast; mortal (of a wound); 5. numeral coefficient for living creatures’ (OJED s.v.). I assume that the word bīra here is the other form of vīra which is refers to brave man, hero, valiant warrior; brave, valiant (OJED s.v.). This phenomenon is often in Old Javanese, for instance the word bulan ‘moon’ also has other form as vulan.There […] s.v.). , rich in servants, successful with the king and his minister, [and] you will not be unsurpassed by all your companionsLexically, the sentence tan pada lavan rovaṅta kabeh can be translated as ‘you will not be equal to all your companions’. I translated this sentence more liberal as ‘unsurpassed by all your companions’. .
An interesting textual phenomenon can be observed here. The mss. M, N and U contain the mantra: om̐ mam̐ īśvarāya namaḥ, whereas G contains the mantra: mantra kadi ṅuni, meaning ‘the mantra is as before’. This phenomenon goes beyond lexical synonymy, but is a synonym in syntax scope. The ms. G refers to a previous mantra that already exists in the initial passage (4v-5r), which contains om̐ mam̐ iśvarāya namaḥ.There […] s.v.). , rich in servants, successful with the king and his minister, [and] you will not be unsurpassed by all your companionsLexically, the sentence tan pada lavan rovaṅta kabeh can be translated as ‘you will not be equal to all your companions’. I translated this sentence more liberal as ‘unsurpassed by all your companions’. .

G instead of the word bhāṣa because of the parallel with the MM in passage 5 (hana brata akarvan patrāhāra ṅaranya, pituṅ tahun samayanya, ⟨phalanya⟩ mulih mariṅ svarga saṅ hyaṅ iśvara, sasarnya ajanma riṅ juru basana, sugih hulun, labdha ri saṅ prabhu.). The word basana in was derived from the Sanskrit word vasana ‘clothes, garment, attire’ (see OJED, s.v.). This observance is interesting because it imitates the behavior of Kumbhakarṇa as a young brother of Rāvāṇa in the Rāmāyaṇa epic. On the basis of Kakavin Rāmāyaṇa, the figure of Kumbhakarṇa is always sleeping. However he woke up when he heard the quintessence speech of his grandfather. The Kakavin Rāmāyaṇa mentions the figure of Kumbhakarṇa as follows: Kāla saṅ kaki sәḍәṅ mavara-varah, Kumbhakarṇa sira jagra ya rumәṅə̄, de nikari ujar-ujar pasili-silih, śīghra yar pavuṅu arddha warurutәn. When his grandfather was giving his admonishment, Kumbhakarṇa woke up, and on hearing the conversation quickly became attentive, though still very sleepy (see Santoso, 1980: 358).Furthermore, […] devotion’. is achieved quickly, [and] you will have many disciples.
I have translated the word prih as ‘desire’, as this is its meaning in Balinese (KBI, 2016: 730). OJED (s.v.) defines the word prih as ‘effort, exertion, full attention, great care and devotion’. There […] I have conjectured the word mūrāba as mārab, as the former does not appear in the OJED or Balinese dictionaries. I assume that mūraba is a mystical form of mārab, which means ‘to flare, flame, blaze, glow’ (OJED, s.v.). It is also consistent with the technique of performing the observance, whereby the practitioner eats certain types of flowers. : one should start performing the observance on the fourth day of the waxing moon. One should eat the flower of nāgasāri (Mesua ferrea), pūraṇa (Clitoria ternatea) Nāgasāri: According to the text titled Kavi Jānaki, collected in Unit Lontar, Udayana University. I found the word purāṇa used to designate one plant, namely itil. The text contains: krĕntikā, smaracatrā, wagaprańā, puranā, gamantya ṅa itil (Kavi Jānaki, 16r). In the oral tradition, the word itil refers to the talaṅ flower (Clitoria ternatea)., [and] kulalaṭa I have not found the specific plant to which kulalaṭa refers. OJED (s.v.) explains that lalaṭa is a particular kind of flower or floral motif. . It should end on the full moon. Its result is being handsome [or] beautiful without equal. The mantra is: ’Oṃ hail to Smara! [It is recited] when applying make-up.

This passage does not provide a detailed explanation of the technique for performing the observance. I assume that the word mopavāsa ‘fasting’ is needed here to complete the explanation. The word brata itself also has the meaning of a ‘holy practice’ (fasting, continence, etc.) (OJED, s.v.).There […] I translate aron-aron as ‘half-cooked rice’ rather than ‘with leaves’ (variant form of aron-ron). I assume the word aron-aron was derived from the words haru or aru. In Old Javanese, haru-daṅ means ‘a pot for half-cooked rice’ and paṅarvan means ‘a pot in which half-cooked rice is stirred before being put back in the kukusan’ (ModJ) (OJED, s.v.). In Balinese, the words haru/aru + -an become aruwan/aron (another instance for this sound change is: kalaṅvan → kalaṅon/kalaṅәn, vvaṅ → voṅ, etc. ), meaning ‘half-cooked rice’. , [and] burning coconuts. Its appointed duration is fifteen days. The deity of the observance is the Reverend Viśeṣa. Its result is a beautiful head.
I translate aron-aron as ‘half-cooked rice’ rather than ‘with leaves’ (variant form of aron-ron). I assume the word aron-aron was derived from the words haru or aru. In Old Javanese, haru-daṅ means ‘a pot for half-cooked rice’ and paṅarvan means ‘a pot in which half-cooked rice is stirred before being put back in the kukusan’ (ModJ) (OJED, s.v.). For the reason in adding the word pha, in this passage see footnote 3.331.There […] I have added the word pha, meaning ‘its result’ in accordance with the general pattern found in other passages of the Tattva Brata. Pha is typically placed after the mantra portion: ma, om̐ śambhave namaḥ, pamit, pha, mañjanma riṅ kulaputra (3.26); after the duration of the brata: tigaṅ tahun lavasnya, pha, drәman aputra, siṅ prih meṅgal katəkan (3.27); after the technical details of the brata’s performance: hana brata tan pamaṅan ivak bavi, pha, tan kataman deniṅ sarvaviṣya (3.63), after the name of the brata: saṅ hyaṅ kr̥ta bhuvana hyaṅniṅ brata, pha, etc. (3.87). is being happy in your journey; the ash of your trace is followed by attendants; you will be successful with happiness and wealth; you will enjoy the palace in the future.
